This two-pack of Tile Stickers have an adhesive back, so you can stick them to your essentials and keep track of them, like your keys, wallet and remote. You can pair them with the Tile app to track their most recent location and ring the device if needed.
Best Amazon Black Friday beauty and wellness deals
Medicube Toner Pads Zero Pore Pad 2.0

These TikTok-beloved toner pads are a favorite among our editors, who tested them for our Medicube brand guide. The pads are dual-sided: one side is textured to exfoliate, while the other is soft to hydrate and soothe your skin. NBC Selected senior editor Nikki Brown, who uses these pads to treat her hormonal acne, says the textured side feels gentle on her skin, so there’s no burning sensation during or after she uses it. They also come with a pair of small tongs, so you don’t have to use your fingers to separate the pads.
Crest 3D Whitestrips Professional Effects

One of our favorite at-home teeth-whitening products, this pack comes with 20 treatments that gently brighten your teeth over time and keep them white for at least 12 months, according to the brand. Crest recommends using the strips once a day for 30 minutes. The kit also comes with two one-hour express treatments you can use when you’ve got a bit more time.
Shark DePuffi

The viral Shark DePuffi has a gua sha-inspired edge and six customizable temperatures that go from cold to hot. I use this device nearly every day and notice it makes me look so much less puffy and more awake in the morning. As you massage it along your face and neck, it depuffs, sculpts and temporarily relieves muscle tension. It comes with a charger and travel case, so you can take it on the go.
Biodance Bio-Collagen Real Deep Mask

Biodance’s sheet masks have hyaluronic acid to hydrate and moisturize skin. I use these at least once a week and love how it goes from opaque to completely translucent overnight. My skin feels soft, smooth and hydrated as soon as I take it off in the morning.
Nodpod Mineralized Silk Gentle Pressure Sleep Mask

The Nodpod is essentially a weighted blanket for your eyes. I have the original Nodpod and loved it so much that I got the silk version, which is much gentler on my sensitive skin. Plus, as a hot sleeper, I love that the silk feels cool. It’s machine-washable and doesn’t use straps, velcro or tension like most sleep masks, which makes it feel much less constricting.
Cosrx Snail Mucin 96% Repairing Face Serum

This buzzy ingredient hydrates skin and targets fine lines, according to experts in our guide to snail mucin. This Cosrx serum, one of our favorite facial essences, is suitable for all skin types, lightweight and hypoallergenic, according to the brand.
Best Amazon Black Friday travel and outdoor deals
Shark ChillPill

This portable fan came in handy during the hotter months, and I always carry it around in my purse or work tote in case I need a boost of cold air. It has 10 speeds, which is more than many other popular handheld fans I’ve tried, and a compartment for water that allows it to both function as a mister and activate the cooling plate on the side. I place the cooling plate directly on my neck to help lower my skin temperature on particularly hot days.
Stanley Quencher H2.0 Flow State 40-Ounce Tumbler

Our editors agree that the Stanley Quencher withstands the test of time. It keeps drinks cold and ice frozen for hours thanks to its stainless steel construction and double-walled vacuum insulation. The base is cup holder-friendly and you can move the lid to drink, place a straw or completely cover the top. The large handle also makes it comfortable to hold wherever you go.

This viral active play system that gets kids and families moving. It has a growing library of 60+ games from major brands, including Bluey, Fruit Ninja and Barbie. This 3D pen set has no hot parts, so it’s safe for children ages 6 and up to create 3D doodles, structures and more. The set comes with a doodle pad, 72 strands of mixed-color plastics, a USB-C cable and an activity guide to get them started.

This set comes with 100 magnetic tiles.

The Owlet Dream Sock is a popular wearable smart monitor that tracks your baby’s pulse rate, blood oxygen levels and sleep patterns in real time. title: Talking Shop with comedian Heather McMahan
summary: Comedian Heather McMahan is going on tour in 2027. She’s not traveling without her favorite packing cubes, snacks, lashes and compression socks.
story: Talking Shop is our series where we talk to interesting people about their most interesting buys.

One of the things Heather McMahan has become an expert in throughout her career as a comedian is traveling. I know that might not totally make sense at first, but when you look at her 2027 schedule alone, you get it. Her Burning Down the House Tour is taking her across the country starting in January,  she’s hosting her Absolutely Knot Cruise in May from Miami to the Bahamas, and somehow between all of that, she’s also recording her podcast and making it back home to Atlanta as much as possible. McMahan has packing, flying and on-the-go glam down to a science, and turning a hotel room into a home is her specialty.

Because she’s such a travel professional, McMahan recently partnered with Hilton to debut its New Ways to Stay campaign, which included a pop-up experience in New York City’s Time Square and a vacation sweepstakes that sent six people on surprise solo getaways. I got to talk to McMahan at the pop-up, who told me that while there’s numerous luxury amenities at Hilton locations worldwide, there’s one she looks forward to the most.

“I know you’re expecting me to say a nice gym,” she joked, “but I actually love that perfect 5 p.m. happy hour moment where you’re sitting in a great cocktail bar in a gorgeous hotel and you’re having your aperol spritz or whatever your drink of choice is — even if it’s a Diet Coke with a lime in it. You’re sitting there and you’re like, ‘We’re here. We arrived. Look at all the things we’ve done in this brand-new city or destination that we’ve been in today.’”
McMahan also gave me a rundown of her travel essentials, including the top four things she brings for her dressing room while she’s on tour.
Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter.
Weezie Packing Cube Bundle (3 pieces)

“When I’m packing, I have every intention of keeping things organized. It’s all in the cubes, and then my husband calls me Hurricane Heather because when I get to a hotel, everything explodes out of my bag,” says McMahan. “He’s like, ‘Heather, this is the most organized chaos.’ But I know where my stuff is. It’s in the bags, that are in the other bags, that are in the cubes, that are shoved somewhere. Just don’t touch it.”

If there’s one thing McMahan will admit to over-packing, it’s underwear. “Listen, I’m going to tell you right now: pack more underwear than you think, alright? Just grab a handful and at least throw an extra 10 in there because you never know,” she says. “But whatever you forgot at home, Hilton’s got it, so call down to the front desk, and be like, “Hi, I need a toothbrush kit.” Come on — they’re thinking three steps ahead. You think this is their first rodeo? They know what’s going on.”
Spanx AirEssentials Half Zip

“I like to look nice on an airplane, so I’m always going to have a nice jacket, a blazer or a cashmere sweater,” says McMahan. “It’s freezing on airplanes, so it’s a way to kind of pull yourself together. You can have sweats on underneath, but just have a nice blazer or cashmere sweater.” One of her favorite sweaters to throw on is Spanx’s AirEssentials Half Zip, which is made from lightweight, silky-soft fabric to keep her cozy.
All in Motion Women’s Essential Compression Socks

McMahan also always wears compression socks to help with circulation on an airplane, especially because she often flies multiple times a week. She loves All in Motion’s Women’s Essential Compression Socks from Target, which comes in a two pack. They’re lightly cushioned, extend up to the knees and have a wide cuff, making them easy to put on and take off. There’s built-in arch support, too.
We can help you find
Barebells Salty Peanut Protein Bars

That’s just what I do,” says McMahan. She’s low maintenance about her in-flight entertainment, but she doesn’t mess around when it comes to snacks.

“You do not want to see me panicking if you think my blood sugar has gotten low, so I’ve always got some sort of sweet treat and a protein snack,” says McMahan. I like to decompress before I turn it on, so I listen to a very specific Spotify playlist called ‘Cocktail Jazz.’ Then I do a full glam beat, and then I eat a hunk of cheese and a handful of salami, and chug a Spindrift — that’s what I do before a show. title: Fiona the hippo dies after eating a hat that ended up in her habitat, Cincinnati Zoo says
summary: Cincinnati Zoo’s beloved hippo Fiona has died following complications from eating a hat that was tossed by a visitor and ended up in her enclosure, the zoo announced Thursday.
story: Cincinnati Zoo’s beloved hippo Fiona has died following complications from eating a hat that was tossed by a visitor and ended up in her enclosure, the zoo announced Thursday.
She was 9.

“It is with extreme sadness that we share with you the devastating news that Fiona did not make it after multiple attempts from our amazing vets and keeper team to help her through what ended up being a medical emergency,” the zoo said in a statement.
Fiona had ingested a hat that ended up in her habitat “by accident” last week, zoo officials said.

“Despite multiple attempts to move the hat out of her system, it was ultimately too much to overcome,” the zoo said in a statement. “The team performed necessary supportive care today in an attempt to save her, but it was not successful and she did not recover.”

Fiona’s care team had tried multiple approaches to help her, including a having the hippo stand on a vibration plate with the hope it would encourage movement through her digestive tract, the zoo said.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
“We know everyone in the community will be crushed by this news, as we all are,” the statement said.
The zoo asked the public to keep her caretakers in their thoughts.

The knit hat got into Fiona’s habitat after it was tossed into the air by a visitor and got caught by a ceiling fan that catapulted it through a small opening above the area’s viewing windows, The Associated Press reported, citing zoo spokesperson Michelle Curley.
Hippos are primarily herbivores with diets largely of grass.
Dr. Gabriella Flacke, an associate veterinarian at Zoo Miami with expertise in hippos, told NBC News the hat was likely made of synthetic material that was not digestible to begin with.
“It probably was trying to move through her intestines in much of the original state that it was in when it was ingested, and that clearly was too big to fit,” she said.
Flacke said the hat could have soaked up fluid from her intestinal tract and became “more thickened and swollen.”
“It didn’t fit through the intestine was basically what happened and and it couldn’t be broken down either,” she added.
Experts will determine what happened when they conduct a necropsy.

Flacke said there have been cases of hippos eating something they shouldn’t have, and most of those cases “resulted in the hippos not making it.” However, there have been instances in which the objects came out on the other side in their feces.
She said surgery wasn’t an option for Fiona and would have been extremely high-risk.

“Just because of the animal’s very large size, the pressure on the abdomen from their intestines, putting a lot of pressure on any type of incision that you would make. Also, the skin being very, very thick and not having like the same sort of anatomy as other mammal skin, like a dog or a horse or us, for example, doesn’t heal very well,” she said.
Flacke remembered Fiona as “such a charismatic animal” who “had a really rough start in life and then beat all the odds.”
Fiona became a global celebrity soon after her premature birth nearly a decade ago.

She was born six weeks early in January 2017 and the world followed her progress online, rooting for the baby hippo to survive. Fiona quickly became a star: Books were written about her, she inspired a line of beer, and a couple got engaged in front of her exhibit.
Cincinnati Mayor Aftab Pureval posted a tribute mourning Fiona’s passing.

“Fiona was a symbol of perseverance and joy in Cincinnati. She brought smiles to so many faces, from kids to parents to visitors from around the world,” he said on X. “Our city is heartbroken, but we couldn’t be more grateful that she was part of our lives and our community as a whole.”

title: Trump’s pick for agency providing election security says Jan. 6 was not an attack
summary: The nominee selected by President Donald Trump to lead the agency tasked with protecting elections in the U.S. refused Thursday to answer who won the 2020 presidential election or call the riot on Jan. 6, 2021, “an attack.”
story: The nominee selected by President Donald Trump to lead the agency tasked with protecting elections in the U.S. refused Thursday to answer who won the 2020 presidential election or call the riot on Jan. 6, 2021, “an attack.”

Michael LoSapio, who is nominated to lead the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, was pressed by Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., on the issues during a confirmation hearing before the Senate Homeland Security Committee.
Asked specifically who won the presidential race in 2020, LoSapio said, “I’m not going to answer the question about an election six years ago.”
“My only involvement in the 2020 election was voting for the president of the United States,” he added, referencing Trump.
Blumenthal accused LoSapio of “ducking the question in a way that betrays your lack of independence and objectivity.”
CISA has not had a director confirmed by the Senate since Trump returned to office in January 2025, when Jen Easterly vacated the role.
The agency, which was established during the first Trump administration, was meant to protect the country’s critical infrastructure, including its elections, from hackers or cybercriminals.
For Subscribers
LoSapio, who serves as the chief information security officer at data and software company Palantir, was also asked whether there was an attack on the Capitol on Jan. 6.
Blumenthal pressed him on the issue, saying, “You don’t know?”
“No, I don’t believe it was an attack,” LoSapio said. “I wasn’t involved in politics. I know what I saw on the news.”
Blumenthal asked LoSapio about the nature of the riot once again, to which he maintained that “it was not an attack.”
For Subscribers
Trump’s own account of Jan. 6 has changed over the years, as he initially sought to distance himself from the riot, calling what happened “acts of violence and destruction” on Jan. 7, 2021.

Though, as he hit the campaign trail in 2024, Trump shifted gears to call it a “day of love,” and later, when he returned to office, he pardoned roughly 1,500 people and commuted the sentences of another 14 in connection with the attack. Trump’s Justice Department also tried to launch a controversial “anti-weaponization” fund, which critics have called a “slush fund” to compensate the president’s allies.
LoSapio is one of 13 nominees who appeared before the committee Thursday seeking to take over federal oversight, inspector general, Postal Service and District of Columbia Superior Court positions.

To be confirmed as CISA director, LoSapio requires the committee to vote to advance his nomination to the full Senate, whose vote by a simple majority will determine whether he is confirmed. The clock is ticking for Trump nominees, as Democrats will take over control of Congress in January.
The result of the 2020 presidential election has shaped CISA’s leadership. Trump fired its first director, Chris Krebs, just weeks after the election over his assertion that it was a secure race.
LoSapio isn’t the first Trump nominee to skirt around questions regarding 2020’s presidential race.
On Wednesday, Cody Hiland, Trump’s pick for a federal appeals court seat, told Blumenthal, “I’m not going to answer that,” when asked who won the election.
Asked why he would not answer, Hiland said, “Because it’s going down a political track on an issue that happened six years ago, and I don’t want to come close to an ethical violation.”
“We know the White House told you, ‘Don’t answer that question,’” Blumenthal responded.

title: Senate passes bill simplifying permitting rules to build in America, sending it to House
summary: The Senate voted 62-33 on Thursday night to pass a sweeping bill to simplify and overhaul permitting rules for energy and infrastructure projects.
story: WASHINGTON — The Senate voted 62-33 on Thursday night to pass a sweeping bill to simplify and overhaul permitting rules for energy and infrastructure projects.

The bill, called the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, was crafted by an unusual coalition of Sens. Shelley Moore Capito, R-W.Va.; Sheldon Whitehouse, D-R.I.; Mike Lee, R-Utah; and Martin Heinrich, D-N.M.

The legislation would revise and speed up environmental reviews with tighter deadlines; accelerate electricity transmission; restrict the power of federal agencies to revoke existing permits; and reduce chokepoints for approving and completing projects.
To conservatives, it’s about cutting government bureaucracy.

“For far too long, critical investments in our nation’s infrastructure, energy production, and economy have been forced to sit on the sidelines due to endless red tape, duplicative reviews, and regulatory uncertainty,” Capito said.
For liberals, it’s an opportunity to make it easier to build long-sought projects, including clean energy, and address high costs.
“Democrats are focused on lowering energy costs, reducing emissions, and stopping data centers’ free ride,” Whitehouse said. “Americans will start to get some relief quickly if this bill passes.”

In an attempt to alleviate Americans’ concerns about data centers, the bill would require “new data centers of 20 megawatts or more to pay the full incremental cost of the infrastructure built to serve them,” according to the Bipartisan Policy Center.

The legislation sparked opposition from some environmental groups and Native American tribal organizations, which objected to easing reviews and consultation rules that can be used to protect their interests. The bulk of the opposition in the Senate came from Democrats.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

Still, the willingness to simplify permitting rules represents a philosophical shift for the Democrats who endorsed it. Part of the reason is that liberal policy experts recognized that existing laws hinder their own goals.

“This removes a lot of the obstacles that hamstrung [Joe] Biden’s climate investments,” said Adam Jentleson, a former Senate Democratic aide and founder of the research group Searchlight Institute. “A big part of the Inflation Reduction Act — a lot of the projects couldn’t break ground because of all the red tape.”
The bill still needs approval from the House, where Majority Leader Steve Scalise, R-La., expressed optimism that Congress will send a bill to President Donald Trump’s desk.

“Well, we want to see a bill pass both chambers,” Scalise said when asked if the House will take up the Senate version of the legislation. “Obviously, the details matter. ... Hopefully, they pass a good bill back, and if not, we’ll work out those differences. But we want to get a bill to the president’s desk, and that’s still got a great chance to happen.”
Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., said the clearest path to making a law is for the House to take the Senate’s measure and pass it, noting that it has been through extensive debate.

“It has been litigated now for months. Continues to be,” Thune told reporters. “Everything gets more complicated over here procedurally, and if it were to go over there and then come back over here, I can’t predict what happens. So hopefully there’ll be the critical mass there to move it. ... It’s been through the full monty when it comes to the legislating process.”

title: Trump gives posthumous pardon to baseball’s Pete Rose, who pleaded guilty to tax evasion
summary: The baseball great, who died in 2024, pleaded guilty to federal tax evasion charges in 1990 and had been banned from the sport for betting on games.
story: President Donald Trump announced on social media Thursday that he has pardoned the late Pete Rose, baseball’s all-time hits leader.

“I have just given a Complete and Total Pardon to the Late, Great Pete Rose, a true Baseball SUPERSTAR & LEGEND, whose record of 4,256 Hits in a Season will never be broken,” Trump said in a post on Truth Social as he was returning from a meeting in China with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Rose had 4,256 hits in his major league career, not in a single season. Trump’s post was later edited to correct that achievement.
Trump added that Rose “was treated terribly by Major League Baseball in not allowing him to go into the Baseball Hall of Fame.”

Rose died in 2024 at age 83. He pleaded guilty to federal tax evasion charges in 1990 and had been permanently banned from baseball after he gambled on his own team as a player and manager. That ban was posthumously lifted last year after repeated requests from Trump.
MLB Commissioner Rob Manfred said at the time that permanent ineligibility “ends upon the passing of the disciplined individual.”
Trump, who’d advocated for Rose’s inclusion in the Baseball Hall of Fame for years, announced his plans to pardon Rose in March 2025.
“He never betted against himself, or the other team. He had the most hits, by far, in baseball history, and won more games than anyone in sports history,” Trump said then.
Rose denied he’d gambled on baseball for almost 15 years before admitting in his 2004 autobiography that he’d bet both as a player and a manager, but never against his own team.
Rose played 24 seasons in Major League Baseball, the last three as a player-manager for the Cincinnati Reds, where he played for the bulk of his career.
The National Baseball Hall of Fame has said that Rose’s removal from the ineligible list means his candidacy can be considered when its Classic Baseball Era Committee meets in December of next year.

title: Troy Aikman escalates feud with Joe Buck, says he ‘always wanted a one-man booth’
summary: This NFL season was supposed to be a celebration for ESPN, as it prepares to host its first Super Bowl.
story: This NFL season was supposed to be a celebration for ESPN, as it prepares to host its first Super Bowl. Instead, the spotlight remains on the network’s top football broadcast booth over the tension between longtime partners Joe Buck and analyst Troy Aikman.

While Buck re-signed with ESPN on a long-term, lucrative contract in September, Aikman has been working without an extension to a deal that is set to expire in 2027. The potential breakup of the broadcast team that has worked together for a quarter-century sparked a reported argument in October, and on Thursday Aikman turned up speculation while calling out Buck during his weekly appearance on a Dallas sports radio station.
“I know Joe’s always wanted a one-man booth,” Aikman told 96.7 The Ticket.

Aikman and Buck had spent two decades working together calling games for Fox before they each arrived at ESPN in 2022 as part of an overhaul of the network’s flagship “Monday Night Football” broadcast. Both arrived on five-year contracts. As this season began, Buck told Front Office Sports in September that “Troy Aikman knows that I have his back. … He knows I’m his biggest fan, vice versa.”

Days later, numerous outlets reported Buck had re-signed with the network on a six-year contract worth more than $100 million. Aikman’s deal was set to expire after the Super Bowl. Signs of discord over Buck’s job security at ESPN, and Aikman’s lack of a guaranteed future there, first became public when outlets reported the two had argued before calling an Oct. 12 game between the Buffalo Bills and Los Angeles Rams.
The Athletic later reported that prior to Buck and Aikman’s argument, Aikman had met with ESPN chairman Jimmy Pitaro about his future and his relationship with Buck.

“There’s probably a time and a place for all that,” Aikman said of dynamic with Buck on Oct. 15. “I don’t know if now is the time. I don’t know if it’s hard to figure out kind of what happened. I’ll broadcast through this season and I’ll be a free agent at the end of the year and kind of see what happens. I’m looking forward to whatever the rest of this season does hold and the Super Bowl and all that and where my next landing spot may be.”
Pitaro called the timing of media coverage of Buck and Aikman’s falling out “disappointing,” as February’s Super Bowl will be ESPN’s first.

“They’ve done a great job for ESPN, they’ve done a great job for the league, they’ve done a great job for the game, and most importantly, they’ve done a great job for fans. Are we happy about the media coverage recently? Of course not. It’s been disappointing,” Pitaro said this week. “But these guys are professionals, and they’re delivering every week. If you watched it last night, another super high-quality production and telecast, and I’d fully expect that to continue that through the season and through the Super Bowl.”

title: How a rocket scientist is fueling the NFL’s best defense
summary: The Minnesota Vikings’ defense is the top-rated unit in the entire NFL — and a former rocket scientist may be the reason why.
story: The Minnesota Vikings’ defense is the type of unit that unleashes pure terror on its opponents, a whirring buzz saw of blitzes coming from all levels of the field and entirely unpredictable.

It leads the NFL in total touchdowns allowed (just 12 scores this season), average points allowed per game (14) and total number of sacks (37) — a testament to making life quite miserable for opposing quarterbacks.

But one of the untold secrets of their success might be that acclaimed defensive coordinator Brian Flores happily accepts input from all corners, and that includes rocket scientists. In this case, it’s the team’s assistant defensive backs coach, Chenzo Funari, who until a few years ago was working on SpaceX’s combustion devices group and the company’s Starship system.
The 32-year-old said he questioned whether the role was “bringing me kind of the fulfillment in life that I thought it would.”

title: Anthropic shares tank after huge IPO, as markets struggle to shake off a bad week
summary: A bruising stock market sell-off looked set to continue despite a record-setting IPO by Anthropic and hopes it would revive sentiment on the AI trade.
story: A bruising stock market sell-off appeared to be gathering steam Friday morning, despite high hopes that Anthropic’s record-setting IPO a day earlier would revive sentiment around the flagging AI trade.
Instead, Friday’s early downturn was led by Anthropic itself, whose shares were down 10% after rising 17% on its first day on the Nasdaq Composite.
The S&P 500 was trading 1% lower as it headed for its worst losing week since April 2025, when President Donald Trump announced his “Liberation Day” tariffs.
Meanwhile, the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite was off more than 2%. Other major AI-related names such as CoreWeave, Nvidia and Oracle also fell in the premarket.

The six consecutive declining S&P 500 sessions mark the index’s longest losing streak since April 2024. A seventh losing day would make it the longest stretch since the pandemic slump in February 2020, according to Deutsche Bank.
For U.S. households relying on 401(k)s and pension funds for retirement, the downturn is especially unwelcome at a time when inflation continues to prove stubborn.

Given the importance the AI trade has played this year in propelling markets and economic growth writ large, its derailment amid concerns about costs, debt, profitability and political risk could have broader implications.
Investor concerns about AI revenues tied to exports of advanced technology to China compounded the sell-off.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

The Jensen Huang scandal pulling down Nvidia appeared to broaden Thursday, when a short-selling firm issued a report raising questions about whether Advanced Micro Devices, another chip giant, may also have had shipments to Asia diverted to mainland China.

Alongside the stock sell-off, there has been an increase in purchases of U.S. Treasury bonds — a sign that investors are seeing signs of weakening growth amid higher interest rates from the Federal Reserve and a stalling economy in China.
“The pressure is becoming increasingly widespread, and that’s been felt across other asset classes too,” Deutsche Bank managing director Jim Reid wrote in a note to clients Friday.

Kevin Gordon, head of macroeconomic strategy and research at Charles Schwab, told NBC News that markets are feeling particular pressure from an increasingly “hawkish” Federal Reserve that is signaling aggressive rate hikes in the face of unrelenting inflation.
“They’re signaling that they want to be aggressive in raising rates,” Gordon said. Combined with a weeks-long downturn among AI and tech stocks, “we have dual forces hitting the market.”
Gaurav Mallik, chief investment officer at New Jersey-based Modera Wealth Management, called the recent sell-off “a garden-variety correction.”
But he noted that overall returns have still been respectable this year, “especially against a challenging backdrop of rising rates, persistent inflation and fears about an AI slowdown.”
But a prolonged downturn could begin to cut more deeply into economic growth.
“If you have enough of a protracted downturn, which we really haven’t had since 2007-2009 in terms of length and duration, that’s when you’d really start to worry,” he said.

title: Deadly Russian strikes hit 3 Kyiv bridges after Putin vows revenge for Crimea attacks
summary: Three bridges in Kyiv were hit in a Russian ballistic missile attack, officials in the Ukrainian capital said, after President Vladimir Putin vowed revenge.
story: KYIV, Ukraine — Three bridges in Kyiv were hit in a massive Russian ballistic missile attack, officials in the Ukrainian capital said Friday, hours after President Vladimir Putin vowed “painful” revenge for strikes on his prized bridge linking Crimea to Russia.

The attacks, which started in the early hours of the morning and continued well into the day damaged the Podilsko-Voskresenskyi, Darnytskyi and Southern bridges connecting the left and right banks of the Dnipro River, which flows through the city, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said in a post on Telegram.

At least six people were killed and 15 injured in the strikes on the capital, Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi said in a separate post. Two others were killed in separate attacks across the country, which saw nine regions hit overnight, he said.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

The strikes on Kyiv forced authorities to restrict traffic on the bridges, impacting the movement across the capital, and Klitschko asked residents not to drive private cars into the city “unless absolutely necessary” and suggested employers should let staff work remotely.

Russia has been hitting Kyiv’s Southern and Northern bridges since early October, causing multiple closures, disrupting metro services and causing traffic jams — complicating day-to-day life in the city that’s home to millions of people.
But it is the first time that Russia hit three different bridges in a single night, and it has left most of the main road crossings over the Dnipro damaged or restricted at the same time.
An NBC News team in Kyiv heard air raid sirens going off every few minutes overnight, accompanied by loud explosions.
After dawn broke on the rainy and foggy Friday morning, firefighters were seen putting out the flames from a strike on an industrial area in the capital.
It’s part of the daily reality for Kyiv’s residents after Russia escalated both the number of ballistic missiles it was firing at the capital and the frequency of attacks.
The latest strikes came hours after Putin said that Moscow would hit back hard after Ukraine struck the Kerch Bridge linking Russia and Crimea for a third time this week.

title: Palestinians flee as Israeli tanks cross Gaza ceasefire’s ‘yellow line’
summary: Israel’s ground operation across the yellow ceasefire line in Gaza, which forced Palestinians to flee their makeshift shelters, marks a fresh escalation in the conflict and risks undermining an already floundering truce with Hamas, analysts said Thursday.
story: Israel’s ground operation across the yellow ceasefire line in Gaza, which forced Palestinians to flee their makeshift shelters, marks a fresh escalation in the conflict and risks undermining an already floundering truce with Hamas, analysts said Thursday.

As tanks rolled into central Gaza on Wednesday, residents could be seen carrying blankets and other belongings away from their tents in pictures and video taken shortly after the Israeli military began what it said was an operation targeting a “terror tunnel.”

Others could be seen rolling away mattresses on carts and pushing loved ones in wheelchairs away from the scene near the Nuseirat camp in central Gaza. At least one person was reported to have been killed in an Israeli airstrike near the raid, Palestinian medics said, according to Reuters.

“Bullets were fired at us,” Amna al-Gasar, 49, told NBC News after she fled the scene with her young children, her baby in a pink fluffy sweater strapped to her chest. She said her family had received “evacuation orders” from the Israeli military and that tanks had advanced on the area.

“This is the 14th time that we’re getting displaced,” al-Gasar said, who added that she is from Gaza City in the north of the enclave which is now on the side of the “yellow line” occupied by Israeli forces. “Where should we go? We are exhausted. This is not a life,” she said.

Muna Abu Shehadeh, 37, said in a separate interview that along with some of her relatives, she left “with nothing but our children — no bedding, no food, and no water.” She added that she had a daughter who was ill, as well as a baby, and that they had to leave behind what few supplies they had.

The Israeli military told NBC News the ground operation was the first to be executed beyond the yellow line — the boundary marking the roughly 60% of Gaza that remains occupied by Israeli forces — since the U.S.-brokered ceasefire with Hamas came into effect in October 2025.

Separately, in a joint statement with the Israel Security Agency, or Shin Bet, the Israel Defense Forces said the operation was a “targeted” assault aimed at dismantling a tunnel that “posed an immediate and direct threat” to troops.

title: Larry Poindexter, ‘Days of Our Lives’ and ‘S.W.A.T.’ actor, dies after being hit by car
summary: Veteran actor Larry Poindexter — who appeared in soap operas “Days of Our Lives” and “General Hospital” and the movie “S.W.A.T.”
story: Veteran actor Larry Poindexter — who appeared in soap operas “Days of Our Lives” and “General Hospital” and the movie “S.W.A.T.” — died Wednesday, days after he was hit by a car while crossing the street near his Los Angeles home, officials said Thursday.
He was 66.

Poindexter was walking near the corner of Moorpark Street and Lankershim Boulevard on Friday, about three blocks from the actor’s home, when he was struck by a car at around 6 p.m. PT, his agent and police said.
The investigation is ongoing, an LAPD spokesperson said.
“He was picking up some dinner,” the actor’s agent, Harry Gold, told NBC News on Thursday.
Poindexter suffered broken ribs but his injuries were not believed to be fatal, according to Gold.
“They did not diagnose this as anything serious,” Gold said. “They put him in the hospital for observation and to repair some broken bones and then he passed away.”
Gold praised his client’s work ethic and diverse skill set.
“He had great musical talent, was in rock band and produced musicals,” Gold said. “That was important to him.”
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
Poindexter’s long career includes 30 episodes on “Days of Our Lives” between 1984 and 2018 and a dozen appearances on “General Hospital” in 2005.
He played by-the-book LAPD Capt. Tom Fuller in the 2003 movie “S.W.A.T.,” supervising Samuel L. Jackson’s Sgt. Dan “Hondo” Harrelson.

“He offered wisdom I wasn’t always ready to hear, and it took me a few years to realize just how right he was about so many things,” Iacono wrote. “He taught me that being a good person and collaborator mattered just as much as being a great actor.”

Iacono posted a picture of himself flanked by his on-screen parents, Poindexter and Beth Littleford, adding that: “I’m forever honored to have played his son, and I’ll always cherish him as my second father.”
Poindexter is survived by his wife, casting director Carol Kritzer, and their twin boys, Rees and Jake.

title: Jax Taylor, former ‘Vanderpump Rules’ star, reveals cancer diagnosis
summary: Jax Taylor, who was made famous on the Bravo reality series “Vanderpump Rules,” shared with fans Thursday that he was recently diagnosed with cancer.
story: Jax Taylor, who was made famous on the Bravo reality series “Vanderpump Rules,” shared with fans Thursday that he was recently diagnosed with cancer.

Taylor, 47, wrote on his Instagram account that he’d been seeking treatment for what he believed was kidney stones in July when a CT scan showed a tumor above his left kidney. He sought care because he woke up one morning “in horrible pain,” he said, adding that the cancer was diagnosed after “many tests and appointments.”
“I lost my father to cancer, so hearing that word just broke me,” Taylor wrote. “It put me in a really dark place.”

The tumor was removed in a five-hour surgery, with Taylor saying the growth was larger than initially expected. He expressed his gratitude to medical staff at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center, in Los Angeles, for all their care.

Taylor described the ordeal as an eye-opening experience that reminded him how quickly life can change. In his statement, Taylor also noted that he will be two years sober next week and said he was proud of himself.
“If there’s one thing I hope people can take away from this, it’s never to take your health for granted,” Taylor said. “I did for many years and I won’t ever do that again.”
He did not provide additional details on his diagnosis or his prognosis.

Taylor’s father died in 2017 just weeks after the reality star shared the diagnosis with his fans. He said at the time that he wouldn’t wish the disease on his worst enemy and described his father as his idol.
“My dad was always the person who never got sick, I always looked up to him. I call him all the time,” Taylor said. “To see him so vulnerable, I’ve never seen him emotional my whole entire life.”

Taylor was one of the first cast members to appear in Bravo’s “Vanderpump Rules,” a reality show that revolved around the employees of Lisa Vanderpump’s restaurants. The series was a 2013 spin-off of “The Real Housewives of Beverly Hills,” which Vanderpump starred on for nine seasons.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

He met and married his fellow cast member Brittany Cartwright on the show. The couple were featured in another spinoff, “The Valley,” which followed a number of reality star families going through big changes. Taylor and Cartwright had one child together, a son, before separating in 2024.
As of May, their divorce had not yet been finalized, according to Cartwright.

There were growing concerns from viewers about Taylor’s behavior on the second season of “The Valley.” Cameras captured heated arguments between him and Cartwright before Taylor eventually checked himself into a mental health treatment facility.

Cast members said they received angry messages from Taylor while he was in the facility. Cartwright told viewers that her husband would “rage text” her while there, adding that she worried that if he didn’t receive help he would continue to spiral.
Taylor revealed that he was diagnosed with PTSD and bipolar disorder. The reality star has also been public with his past substance abuse issues, saying he specifically struggled with cocaine use.
He announced last year that he would not return to “The Valley” as he prioritized his mental health.

title: ‘Abbott Elementary’ Star Janelle James Says She ‘Bullied’ Her Way Into a Role in ‘GTA VI’: ‘Dream Come True’
summary: Janelle James of “Abbott Elementary” explains how she landed a role voicing a radio host in “Grand Theft Auto VI.”
story: If you recognize the voice of a certain radio host in the midst of committing motorized mayhem while playing “Grand Theft Auto VI,” you’re not imagining things.
Comedian and “Abbott Elementary” star Janelle James says she “bullied” her way into being included in the blockbuster video game because she is a diehard fan of the “GTA” series.

James is featured as a radio host in the game, which was released to acclaim on Nov. 19 after a 13-year wait since the last edition of “GTA.” She shared the lengths she went to in order to secure her role in a social media post.

“It’s very important to me that everybody knows that not only is that me, I’m not simply ‘voice acting,’” she wrote on her Instagram story Nov. 19. “I pursued, conceptualized, pitched, scripted AND voice acted my radio show.”
James added that she cast comedian friends Zainab Johnson and Liza Treyger on her show on the game, which was created by Rockstar Games.
“Rockstar didn’t ‘choose’ me, I bullied my way to them,” James wrote. “I’ve been playing this game since Vice City and this is a literal dream come true!!”
“Vice City” is an earlier version of the game that was released in 2002.

“GTA VI” allows players to toggle between the characters of Jason, a military veteran with a history of working with drug runners, and his girlfriend, Lucia, a fighter who was recently released from prison. The main characters are voiced by Dylan Rourke and Manni L. Perez.

Gamers had already been speculating that it was James’ voice they were hearing before she confirmed it. James, who plays principal Ava Coleman on “Abbott Elementary,” was instantly recognizable to people playing the game when it first came out.
“Janelle James from Abbott Elementary?!?!?!” one fan wrote on X with a clip from the game with James’ radio show playing.
“Janelle james in gta 6 radio just made this game 100 times better,” another wrote.
“NOT AVA BEING IN GTA 6 LMFAOOO ICONIC,” another posted.
James, 47, also responded to the outpouring of support in her post.
“I’m told the response is already great, TY,” she wrote. “Hope to catch ya’ll in these online streets where I will promptly kick you square in your back then put two in your dome. Cheers!!!”

title: Where Are Sam Bankman-Fried and Caroline Ellison of ‘The Altruists’ Now?
summary: Two of the central figures involved in the collapse of the cryptocurrency exchange FTX into bankruptcy and subsequent trials for fraud have returned to the spotlight four years later.
story: Two of the central figures involved in the collapse of the cryptocurrency exchange FTX into bankruptcy and subsequent trials for fraud have returned to the spotlight four years later.

The new scripted Netflix series “The Altruists,” which begins streaming on Nov. 19, dramatizes the dynamic between Sam Bankman-Fried and his former girlfriend, Caroline Ellison, as they tried to remake the global financial system only for the company to implode in scandal.
Emmy-winning “Ozark” star Julia Garner portrays Ellison, and “Say Nothing” actor Anthony Boyle plays Bankman-Fried in the new series.
Boyle spoke on TODAY Nov. 20 about how he had “a lot of source material” about Bankman-Fried to prepare for the role because of all the interviews he did during FTX’s rise and fall.

“Because there was so much written about him, there was so many different aspects of him from different angles,” Boyle told Craig Melvin, Dylan Dreyer and Al Roker. “So some people thought he was a villain, some people thought he was the white knight of crypto, so I had a lot to draw on.”
Boyle said he also corresponded with Bankman-Fried via email from prison, where Bankman-Fried is serving a 25-year sentence.
“I was really bowled over by his intelligence,” Boyle said. “Even through emails I was like, ‘This guy is a savant.’ He’s so, so clever. Really, really interesting guy.”
Here is what to know about Bankman-Fried and Ellison, how their relationship dissolved, and where they are now.
Who Is Sam Bankman-Fried?
Bankman-Fried, 34, is the co-founder of the Bahamas-based FTX cryptocurrency exchange, which he started in 2019, as well as the crypto trading firm Alameda Research.
FTX became one of the world’s biggest cryptocurrency trading platforms and was valued at more than $30 billion at its peak before filing for bankruptcy in November 2022.

Bankman-Fried, an MIT graduate and son of Stanford professors, also was a prominent figure in the effective altruism movement, which is where the name of the Netflix series “The Altruists” comes from.

Effective altruism is a philosophical movement popular in Silicon Valley that includes the model of “earn to give,” meaning to make as much money as possible in order to give it away for the benefit of mankind, according to NBC News.

The movement is based on the premise that “people ought to do good in the most clear-sighted, ambitious, and unsentimental way possible,” according to a 2022 profile of effective altruism by The New Yorker.

Bankman-Fried ingrained those principles into Alameda Research and FTX, arguing that making large amounts of money would be beneficial because it would then be given away to help others. At one point, his net worth was estimated at $24 billion, according to NBC News.

A slogan that is used in the Netflix series is “all in, all the time,” meaning the altruistic decision is to always pursue the possibility of more money, even if it’s risky, because it can do the most good.

“I think Sam and Caroline both believed that the ends justified the means,” show-runner Graham Moore told Netflix’s Tudum. “Until the FBI showed up, and they found out there was a point at which that doesn’t work anymore.”

When FTX collapsed, Bankman-Fried’s mentor and a leader of the effective altruism movement, Will McAskill, disavowed him. He tweeted in 2022 that if Bankman-Fried “lied and misused customer funds he betrayed me, just as he betrayed his customers, his employees, his investors, & the communities he was a part of.”
Who Is Caroline Ellison?

Ellison, 32, is a Stanford graduate and Bankman-Fried’s former girlfriend and employee. She first met him when they were both working at the Wall Street firm Jane Street out of college in 2016, and she was introduced to the effective altruism movement by him.
She became a trader at Alameda Research in 2018 and then was elevated to co-CEO in 2021, according to a news release by the company.
Ellison and Bankman-Fried began dating in 2020 and broke up in 2022, Bankman-Fried testified at his trial in 2023, according to The Wall Street Journal.
“She wanted more from it than I was able to give,” he said.
What Happened to Sam Bankman-Fried and Caroline Ellison?
Ellison went from being in a romantic relationship with Bankman-Fried to testifying against him during his trial in 2023.

A jury found Bankman-Fried guilty on all seven criminal counts against him in November 2023, which included being convicted of wire fraud and conspiracy to commit wire fraud against FTX customers and against Alameda Research lenders, conspiracy to commit securities fraud and conspiracy to commit commodities fraud against FTX investors, and conspiracy to commit money laundering.

Bankman-Fried, who pleaded not guilty to all the charges, was accused along with other FTX executives of making risky investments with billions of dollars stolen from customer accounts and using funds looted from the company to buy real estate in the Caribbean and make political donations.

Ellison’s lawyers said during her trial that Bankman-Fried had persuaded her to stay at Alameda by saying he loved her and the business needed her “while also perversely demonstrating that he considered her not good enough to be seen in public with him at high-profile events,” according to NBC News.

Ellison cooperated with federal investigators as they built their case against Bankman-Fried. Prosecutors said in a court filing ahead of her sentencing in September 2024 that Ellison’s testimony was “a cornerstone of the trial.”

Her lawyers wrote in the document that Bankman-Fried directed Ellison to help “steal billions” while she lived “in dread, knowing that a disastrous collapse was likely, but fearing that disentangling herself would only hasten that collapse,” according to NBC News.

In December 2022, Ellison accepted a plea deal on charges of financial fraud and conspiracy and cooperated with investigators in outlining the inner workings at FTX and Alameda Research, according to a court filing.
Where is Caroline Ellison Now?
Ellison was sentenced to two years in prison in September 2024 for conspiracy and fraud after taking the plea deal two years earlier.
She had faced a maximum sentence of about 110 years, but received two years due to her cooperation with federal investigators.
U.S. District Judge Lewis A. Kaplan also ordered her to forfeit $11 billion for her involvement in the collapse of FTX.
She began serving her sentence on Nov. 7, 2024, at a federal prison in Danbury, Connecticut, according to The Associated Press.
She did not end up serving the full two years. Ellison was released from federal custody on Jan. 21, 2026 after serving about 14 months, according to records from the Federal Bureau of Prisons.
She then quickly landed a job once she was released and returned to her effective altruism roots.

In a Substack post in September, the founder of Manifund, a philanthropic platform tied to the effective altruism movement, wrote that Ellison had joined the company in August. He wrote that she was hired “to develop our funding platform and research how to effectively direct philanthropic dollars.”
Where Is Sam Bankman-Fried Now?
After being convicted by a jury on all seven criminal counts against him in 2023, Bankman-Fried was sentenced to 25 years in prison in March 2024 for orchestrating the FTX fraud.
In addition to his prison sentence, he was ordered to pay $11 billion in forfeiture.

Bankman-Fried spoke with Tucker Carlson from Brooklyn’s Metropolitan Detention Center in New York City in March 2025, where he shared details about his then-cell block mate Sean “Diddy” Combs and his life in prison.
“It’s sort of dystopian,” Bankman-Fried said. “You know, the fortunate thing, the place I’m in, I’m not in ... I’m not in physical danger.”
In June 2026, a three-judge panel of the Manhattan-based 2nd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals denied his appeal to have his conviction overturned.
He is currently incarcerated at FCI Lompoc I, a low-security federal institution in Lompoc, California, according to the Federal Bureau of Prisons. His release date is listed as Dec. 15, 2043.

title: Beyoncé Sings ‘Irreplaceable’ in Spanish on TODAY in 2007
summary: Beyoncé performed “Irreplaceable” on TODAY in 2007, switching it up and singing it in Spanish.
story: As TODAY marks its 75th anniversary, the TODAY Archive is revisiting legendary interviews, stories that moved us and other iconic moments from our 75 years on the air. These are the segments that shaped TODAY and created a lasting legacy. Today, we look back at Beyoncé singing in Spanish on the plaza on April 2, 2007.
Beyoncé put on a show quite unlike anything fans were expecting when she performed on TODAY on April 2, 2007.

The iconic singer did a rendition of her hit “Irreplaceable,” that featured her adding lyrics from the Spanish-language version “Irreemplazable.” The song was featured in the deluxe edition of “B’Day,” which was released the day after her TODAY appearance.
“How y’all feeling this beautiful morning?” she asked at the top of the performance while perched on a stool, with a guitarist and bassist seated next to her and a band behind them.
Beyoncé Greets the Crowd and Switched Things Up
With a huge crowd surrounding her at the Plaza, the singer kicked off the track by encouraging them to sing along with her.
“I’m doing this acoustic style because I need y’all’s help. Are y’all going to sing this song with me? Y’all know what to do, right? Yeah? Here we go. Sing with me.”
She then launched into “Irreplaceable.”
“Y’all can be a little louder, right?” she said, shortly after starting the song.
She went nearly 90 seconds before she changed things up.
“So, you know what? I want to do something a little different. So I need y’all to be quiet and listen. This right here is for my Latino fans,” she said before singing in Spanish.
Translating the ‘Irreemplazable’ Lyrics
The translation for what she sang veers a little from the English lyrics of the song. Her Spanish lyrics translated to the following:
You see my love, this time I forgot you
In the closet, tucked away in a corner are your things
This is over
I swear I can’t stand you anymore
I don’t want you anymore, neither as a lover
This time you won’t win
You can leave and never come back
And if you think this time I will forgive you
You’ll see that you’ll never deceive me again
Just get out of here
An Energetic Ending and Cheers From the Crowd
She proceeded to sing about 40 seconds in Spanish before going back to English for the chorus and the remainder of the song.
After she finished, the crowd thunderously cheered.

title: ‘The Traitors: New Blood’ Finale Recap: Did the Faithfuls or the Traitors Win?
summary: Read a recap of the two-hour finale of “The Traitors: New Blood” to find out if the Faithfuls were victorious or if the Traitors deceived them and won it all.
story: Warning: Spoilers from the season finale of “The Traitors: New Blood” below…

After weeks of surprising murders and emotional banishments, “The Traitors: New Blood” has come to an end, revealing which player (or players) successfully navigated Alan Cumming’s wicked game and emerged from his castle a winner.

“The Traitors: New Blood,” the first all-civilian season of the reality competition show, wrapped on Thursday, Nov. 19, with an epic two-hour season finale that saw the remaining Faithfuls and Traitors fight for their survival. The season, which was filled with treachery, a tiny Traitor, a mega Traitor, “fruit-gate” and intense Round Table showdowns, saved some of its most thrilling moments for last as the Traitors — Katie and Shane — worked to deceive the Faithfuls one more time.

To make it to the Fire of Truth, the last stage of the game, all the players had to avoid banishment at the remaining two Round Tables, and the Faithfuls had to hope they weren’t the Traitors’ last murder victim.
But after last week’s mission gave the Faithfuls some clues about the Traitors’ identities, Katie and Shane were forced to come up with a risky strategy in the finale to protect themselves.

Did it work? Or did the remaining Faithfuls manage to outlast all the Traitors? Read on for a recap of the supersized finale and find out who joined “The Traitors”’ winner circle nearly $250,000 richer.
The Penultimate Round Table

The first part of the finale, titled “I’m Fighting Till the End,” kicks off with the players returning to the castle after the most recent mission. Clyde begins to test his theory with some of the players that Shane could be a Traitor, sharing that he heard heavy footsteps during the mission. Clyde explains why he suspects Katie is a Traitor, as well. He points out her inability to complete the puzzle in the last mission and notes that the Traitors also struggled to finish their puzzle. Before heading to the Round Table, he asks some of his fellow Faithfuls if they are willing to vote for Katie.

At the Round Table, Alan tells the players that this will be the last time they learn the identity of the player they banish. Shane opens the discussion by criticizing Jay’s strategy throughout the game, revealing that Jay shared his goal was to confuse everyone, including Faithfuls.

When Katie jumps in to make Jay look more suspicious, Clyde suggests that Jay was kept around by the Traitors to be a distraction. He says he believes Katie is a Traitor and mentions the mission puzzle as evidence. Katie admits she isn’t sure how to defend herself before Jay becomes the focus again. Victor points out that Jay voted with the banished Traitors every week and he isn’t open to accepting new information.

All the players vote to banish Jay, who casts a vote for Victor once again, and he is eliminated. On the Circle of Truth, he says, “This has been the ride of my life. I genuinely mean that. When I first came in here, I was a Faithful. But now… I am a Faithful!”
The Traitors’ Final Murder
As the players process the Round Table, Clyde continues to warn them about Katie. He cautions Victor, who confirms he has a crush on Katie, to watch out for her.

In the turret, Shane and Katie discuss their shortlist for murder, which only includes three options since the other players won shields in the previous mission. The two debate whether it is best to remove Victor, Kriste or Clyde from the game.

The final day in the castle arrives. All the players file into the breakfast room except for Clyde, the Traitors’ final casualty of the season. During a flashback, Katie explains that Clyde needed to go because he was coming for both Traitors. She and Shane also hatch a plan to pit Wyatt and Victor against each other before the last Round Table.

When Clyde walks into the confessional and sees a letter from the Traitors waiting for him, he says, “I knew it. Ugh, I’m so sad. But I still think that the Traitors could be Shane and Katie.” Before departing, he adds, “And for all of the Faithful left, don’t let this murder be in vain, ok? Go out there and do what you got to do.”
The Last Mission

For their last mission and final opportunity to add money to the prize pot, the players must locate bunkers around the castle grounds and break into them using dynamite. To do so, they have to split into two teams — one group traveling on wheels and the other via helicopter.

Abbey B. and Katie volunteer to fly high in the helicopter. After directing the group on land to the correct locations, Abbey B. and Katie have to rappel from the side of the helicopter to deliver the dynamite. Despite both having scary moments where they dangled in midair, Abbey B. and Katie complete their task and help raise the prize pot total to $246,300.
The episode ends with Alan advising the players to think about who they can trust.
The Final Round Table

Alan’s ominous words lead into the second part of the finale, fittingly titled “Who Do You Truly Trust?” While preparing for the last Round Table of the season, Victor says he is feeling good. He chats with Shane and Wyatt to confirm that they will all vote to banish Kriste. But during their talk, Victor decides to reveal to Wyatt that he was the player who secretly found a shield in Episode 9. Wyatt is visibly upset that Victor withheld this information from him. Shane says in his confessional that he can use this secret to create tension between Wyatt and Victor.
Wyatt relays his conversation with Victor to Kriste, who then passes it along to Abbey B. Both ladies start to question if Victor is trustworthy.

At the Round Table, Victor says he has been honest the entire game and he is suspicious of Kriste and Katie. Katie is shocked by Victor’s betrayal and says she feels like he has been lying to her. Kriste, meanwhile, rebuffs Victor’s claim that he has been truthful. She calls Victor a liar and a Traitor. “If y’all believe him, you get exactly what you deserve,” she tells her fellow Faithfuls.

But Kriste’s passionate plea has the opposite effect. Some players, including Abbey B., say that Kriste’s intense reaction was out of character and a possible attempt to save herself. Most of the players vote to banish Kriste, who votes for Victor. Katie also joins Kriste in voting to eliminate Victor, which confuses Shane.

Since she cannot reveal her identity, Kriste rises from the table and exits in silence. In her final confessional, she says, “I fought so hard at the end and I was hoping the guys would implode on each other, but they didn’t. It’s just been an amazing ride and it just makes me think what a gift it is to experience all these things in life. And I wouldn’t change a minute of it. I wouldn’t change a second.”
The Fire of Truth

Alan tells the players “one last battle remains”: the Fire of Truth. During their final moments to strategize with each other, Katie says she plans to eliminate Victor so she and Shane can win it all. However, Abbey B. is onto her and tells Wyatt that Katie is a Traitor. Elsewhere, Shane says he wants to finish the game with Katie but he knows the other players do not trust her.

Prior to the Fire of Truth, all the players join Alan for private chats. Shane shares that he wants to win the money so he can take care of his family. Katie explains that she needs the money for security. Victor says he thinks he has what it takes to win, but he needs the other players to trust him. Abbey B. calls the prize money a possible “blessing” that would allow her family to go on a vacation. As for Wyatt, he is more concerned about his allies. He says he doesn’t know if he can count on Victor and that the show has been the most difficult experience of his life.

Alan welcomes the players to the Fire of Truth, where the game will conclude. He explains that the game will end if either they all agree there aren’t any Traitors left or if only two players remain. For the first round, all the players vote to banish again, speculating there is still a Traitor among them. After voting, everyone chooses to eliminate Katie, who votes for Victor.

Katie cries in her confessional as she reflects on her elimination. “I know that wasn’t easy for anyone to do. And it is just a game and I have gained so much from this,” she says. “I am really shocked right now and disappointed in Shane. But I would not change a single thing about this experience other than me losing.”

For the second round, Victor and Shane vote to end the game but Wyatt and Abbey B. want to banish again. They all vote for Victor, who begrudgingly votes for Wyatt. Victor doesn’t have any hard feelings toward his former ally in his exit interview.

“That’s the game right? I got two Traitors out. That’s something I’m proud of,” Victor says in his last confessional. “I got to make some lifelong friends. But sweet, sweet Wyatt, he just couldn’t shake his suspicion of me and I respect it.”

For the third and final round, Wyatt, Abbey B. and Shane vote to end the game. Wyatt becomes emotional and prematurely celebrates their win. Abbey B. is also excited and tells Wyatt and Shane she trusts them. After Wyatt and Abbey B. confirm they are Faithfuls, Shane turns to them and reveals, “I am a Traitor.”

Shane immediately starts apologizing in between sobs. Wyatt and Abbey B. are initially stunned. She then doubles over and weeps. When Wyatt asks for an explanation, Shane says, “I started this game as a Faithful. I was given an ultimatum — either I accept or I get murdered,” adding that he made the choice after Joe was banished. Shane chokes up again before Wyatt and Abbey B. comfort and congratulate him.

In his confessional, Wyatt continues to have a positive attitude. “I really did go into that Round Table believing Shane was a Faithful. A win for the Traitors — that sucks! I am upset about that. But Shane played the perfect game. I can only give him credit,” he says.

Abbey B. is happy for Shane, too. “I am heartbroken and gutted. But you know what? I did the best I could with what I knew,” she shares. “To hear he was a Traitor, I can’t imagine how hard that was for him to look at us and say that. As bad as it hurts, I really am so happy for him. That’s a lot of money! Every single moment of this experience has been magical. So maybe I’m not leaving with the money, but maybe I still win.”

Shane is elated as he celebrates with Alan. “This is life-changing money. I can just finally feel like I’m not drowning under the water. I just feel like I’m barely making it and I can change my life now. Finally, I can actually help people. Thank you so much!” he cheers.
“I did it!” he shouts.
Outside, Shane reunites with the other finalists. Victor says he never expected Shane to be a Traitor. Katie tells Shane she will be ok as long as she gets an invite to his wedding.

After saying everyone is invited to his upcoming nuptials, Shane shares in his last confessional, “I’m so proud of myself. Starting out as a Faithful, then becoming a Traitor, it was so tough. Good things like that don’t really happen to me. This is one of the greatest moments of my life.”

title: Everything We Know About Manni L. Perez, ‘GTA 6’ Female Lead Lucia Caminos
summary: One of the buzziest aspects of the newly released “Grand Theft Auto VI” video game is its introduction of a major playable female character — the first in the “GTA” franchise, which has previously been criticized for its misogynistic content. While developer Rockstar Games has largely kept details about the long-awaited game under wraps, fans this week finally learned the identity of the voice actor behind new character Lucia Caminos.
story: One of the buzziest aspects of the newly released “Grand Theft Auto VI” video game is its introduction of a major playable female character — the first in the “GTA” franchise, which has previously been criticized for its misogynistic content.
While developer Rockstar Games has largely kept details about the long-awaited game under wraps, fans this week finally learned the identity of the voice actor behind new character Lucia Caminos.
Manni Perez, an actor, weightlifter and combat sports athlete, was revealed as the voice actor behind Lucia after she received a Game Awards nomination Nov. 17 for best performance.
Perez has so far not been a large part of the game’s promotion, however she publicly acknowledged her role in “GTA VI” on social media after the news of her nod.
Here’s what we know about Manni Perez.
Perez’s Character Lucia Is a Fugitive
Lucia, one of two characters that players can toggle between, is a a fighter who was recently released from prison and is hoping to thrive on the outside.

“More than anything, Lucia wants the good life her mom has dreamed of since their days in Liberty City — but instead of half-baked fantasies, Lucia is prepared to take matters into her own hands,” the game’s website says.

Together with her boyfriend, Jason, a military veteran who has a history of working with drug runners, Lucia embarks on a Bonnie-and-Clyde-type lifestyle to change her fortunes. However the couple gets caught up in the middle of a criminal conspiracy across the fictional state of Leonida after a robbery goes awry.
Lucia and Jason are then “forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive,” the website says.
Perez Has Made Appearances on Screen, Including in “Law & Order: SVU”
If Lucia’s voice sounds familiar to gamers, it’s likely because they’ve seen Perez before on screen.

The actor, who grew up in New York City and studied at NYU’s Tisch School of the Arts, according to IMBD, has appeared in several high-profile television series, including “Chicago P.D.,” “Blindspot” and Marvel’s “Jessica Jones.”
In a 2020 episode of “SVU,” Perez played Esperanza Morales, a  boxer who was arrested for murder after she attacked her boxing coach, who had been accused of raping a teen.
Perez, who’s a practitioner of MMA, Muay Thai and Brazilian jiu-jitsu, has also worked as a professional belly dancer.
The new game isn’t Perez’s first rodeo with the “Grand Theft Auto” franchise. She previously voiced a blackjack dealer for 2019’s “Grand Theft Auto Online.”
In an interview with the since-shuttered site Paz Magazine, Perez said that that her “biggest fear” was having to portray a “damsel in distress.”

“I’d prefer to play a character that whatever she’s going through, no matter how hard society wants to keep her down, she picks herself up, puts her big girl panties on (preferably cotton [laughs]) and keeps it moving,” she told the outlet.
Perez Has Barely Said Anything About the Game
Perez has said next to nothing about her involvement in the game. It wasn’t until the news of the Game Awards nomination that her identity was revealed.
Still, Perez hasn’t said much about the role aside from sharing a joint post Nov. 19 with the voice actor behind Jason, Dylan Rourke.

“Years witnessing the hardest working and most skilled artisans game making has to offer. We are truly honored to collaborate on this worldwide testament to human creativity, ingenuity, and sheer willpower,” the pair said in a joint Instagram post. “So much learned and so much to learn, keep fighting for what you love, stay humble. See y’all in Leonida.”

title: Burger King Launches Peanuts Menu Featuring Snoopy, Charlie Brown and the Gang
summary: Burger King is partnering with Snoopy, Charlie Brown and the Peanuts gang for its holiday menu, which features loaded tots, cookies & creme pie, and a holiday beanie.
story: Burger King is welcoming the holidays with a rather festive beagle.
On Nov. 19, the burger chain announced a partnership with the Peanuts brand, which has been kicking the football — or at least attempting to — for more than 75 years.

Together, the brands are launching a limited-time menu inspired by Charlie Brown, Snoopy, Woodstock and the rest of the Peanuts gang, starting Tuesday, Dec. 1 at participating U.S. restaurants, while supplies last.
The Peanuts Pack
