Fast Food Is Serving up Nostalgia for the Holidays
Burger King isn’t the only restaurant serving customers a little nostalgia with a side of fries.
On Nov. 16, Wendy’s announced it is offering a holiday meal box based on its iconic ‘80s and ‘90s solariums, along with a collectible retro-style knit beanie.

Then, on Nov. 17, McDonald’s launched its “Home Alone” meal, 36 years after the original film premiered. It comes with pizza-flavored McShaker Fries, a cheese dipping sauce and an over-the-top McFlurry, inspired by Kevin McCallister’s cravings.

title: Taylor Swift Performs ‘I Knew It, I Knew You’ for Her 1st Performance at CMA Awards in 13 Years
summary: Superstar Taylor Swift lit up the stage at the Country Music Association Awards in Nashville, Tennessee Nov. 18 with soulful performance of her single “I Knew It, I Knew You.”
story: Don’t call it a comeback.

Superstar Taylor Swift lit up the stage at the Country Music Association Awards in Nashville, Tennessee Nov. 18 with soulful mashup of her single “I Knew It, I Knew You” and 2006 throwback “Our Song.”
The electric performance marked Swift’s return to the ceremony’s stage 13 years since her last performance. And the crowd was certainly eager to welcome Swift back.
Dressed in a red, ruffled skirt, glittery top and cowboy boots, Swift brought down the house as she strummed her bright blue guitar.

The performance comes over a decade after she last took the stage at the awards show with Vince Gill and Alison Krauss, singing “Red.” At that 2013 ceremony, Swift was also given the Pinnacle Award, a rare accolade that is given to artists who have “undeniably redefined the pinnacle of success in the genre.” It was presented to her by artists she had previously opened for, including Tim McGraw, Faith Hill and George Strait.

After a quick outfit change, Swift returned to the stage later on to present the Willie Nelson Lifetime Achievement Award, an accolade given to the artist who “has attained the highest degree of recognition in Country Music.” Dynamic duo Brooks & Dunn ended up taking home the honor.

Earlier in the night, Swift, a two-time CMA Entertainer of the Year, was also among the nominees for single of the year for “I Knew It, I Knew You,” the singer’s 26th CMA nomination.  Ella Langley ended up winning the accolade with her hit song “Choosin’ Texas.”

But before the ceremony even began, Swift had already made waves across social media for her red carpet look. The singer arrived in a striking yellow strapless gown with a bubble hem from fashion house Oscar de la Renta. She finished the look with gold metallic heels and a classic updo.
“Petition for Taylor to wear yellow more often because she literally looks like a ray of sunshine,” one fan wrote on platform X.
Fans have been awaiting her return to the ceremony after the singer in September wrote in her Instagram stories that she hadn’t “YEED MY LAST HAW” in response to her nomination.

title: See TODAY’s First Weather Forecast Hand-Drawn by Host Dave Garroway in 1952
summary: Original TODAY host Dave Garroway did the first forecast on the show during its first episode on Jan. 14, 1952.
story: As TODAY marks its 75th anniversary, the TODAY Archive is revisiting legendary interviews, stories that moved us and other iconic moments from our 75 years on the air. These are the segments that shaped TODAY and created a lasting legacy. Today, we look back at the very first forecast during the show’s debut broadcast on Jan. 14, 1952.
Before there was Willard Scott or Al Roker, there was Dave Garroway. The original TODAY host was also the first person to do the weather on the show during its premiere episode on Jan. 14, 1952.
While the forecast is one of TODAY’s staples, the first one was a little bit off-kilter, complete with primitive technology that made it a challenge for Garroway. It also shows how far we’ve come.
How Did Dave Garroway Do the Weather?
Garroway was in the studio, chatting on a phone with Jim Fidler, who he said was “with the weather bureau.”
Garroway erased a chalkboard map of the United States while letting viewers in on how Fidler, who was based in Washington, D.C., is helping.

“Jim is our official U.S. weather forecaster, you understand, right  in the weather bureau where they make the stuff,” Garroway said as he readied himself to get Fidler’s information and began to write on the map before technical issues surfaced.
“I can’t hear you on the studio PA,” Garroway said while he fumbled with the phone.
A booming voice from overhead then indicated he’d have to get the information over the phone instead of the PA system, allowing Garroway to repeat what Fidler was saying.
Garroway then wrote out the various forecasts around the country in chalk on the map.
“I want you to know your forecast is very good because it’s raining right here in New York,” Garroway said to Fidler before he carried on writing on the chalkboard, courtesy of his colleague’s notes.
Who Was Jim Fidler?
Fidler, who died in 2007, played a large part in the first forecast, even if viewers couldn’t see or hear him.
He had a deep background in meteorology and radio and his work with TODAY netted NBC the outstanding service award to meteorology from a corporation from the American Meteorological Society in 1953.
That award was given out to the network “for performing an important public service through television coverage of the weather on its network programs,” according to the AMS.
What Did Dave Garroway Say About Doing the Forecast?
At the end of his forecast, Garroway explained how they would normally hear Fidler’s voice over the studio PA.
“Usually, you’ll be able to hear Jimmy’s voice,” he said. “The line to Washington has been a little busy this morning. It didn’t come quite through on time.”
Garroway also assured viewers that mistakes were bound to happen with a new program like TODAY.
“There’ll be lots of bugs on this show, by the way, from time to time. This is a fairly ambitious undertaking. Just expect a few bugs,” he said.

“Like somebody said: We’re like a play in New Haven for the first week. We’re getting ready to come into the big town. Well, we’ll be like that for a while, but don’t mind it ‘cause we don’t mind it.”

title: Pierce Brosnan Congratulates Robert Pattinson on Being Cast As James Bond: ‘You Are Going To Be Magnificent’
summary: Pierce Brosnan, who portrayed James Bond across seven years and four films, welcomed Robert Pattinson into “the world of Bond” in a sweet Instagram post on Nov. 18.
story: Robert Pattinson has received a blessing from 007 himself.

Pierce Brosnan, who portrayed James Bond across seven years and four films, welcomed Pattinson into “the world of Bond” in a sweet Instagram post on Nov. 18. It comes just two days after it was announced that Pattinson would step into the role of the famous British secret agent for the upcoming film.
“Dear Robert, Welcome to the world of Bond,” Brosnan wrote in the post. “You are going to be magnificent.”
Pattinson will portray 007 in the film, which will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, the brains behind the “Dune” trilogy. He will be the seventh person to take on the iconic role.
Brosnan, who portrayed the agent from 1995 to 2002, starred in franchise films “GoldenEye,” “Tomorrow Never Dies,” “The World Is Not Enough” and “Die Another Day.”

In his message to Pattinson, Brosnan reminisced on their shared experience, making the 2010 romantic drama “Remember Me.” Pattinson had portrayed main character Tyler Hawkins while Brosnan played his father Charles Hawkins.
“I have fond memories of our time together making ‘Remember Me,’” Brosnan wrote. “It has been a joy to watch you create a remarkable body of work and to go from strength to strength.”
Brosnan concluded the warm message with a sweet word of advice.
“Enjoy the ride,” Brosnan wrote before signing off with the Gaelic term for “lots of love.” “Grá mor, Pierce”

Fans couldn’t help but chime in on the post, calling for Brosnan’s involvement in the upcoming Bond film. Some demanded Brosnan return as a villain, while others recommended he be cast in the role of M, the mysterious head of the British Secret Intelligence Service.
Whaddya say, Pierce?

title: Lainey Wilson, Vince Gill Open the CMA Awards With a Powerful Dolly Parton Tribute
summary: The Queen of Country just got a royal tribute at the Country Music Awards.
story: The Queen of Country just got a royal tribute at the Country Music Awards.

The ceremony, which kicked off in Nashville, Tennessee Nov. 18, opened with an emotional performance by Lainey Wilson and Vince Gill, singing the Parton’s smash hit “I Will Always Love You in a dazzling homage to Dolly Parton. The late singer, a trailblazing force in the country music genre, died in August after a brief battle with cancer.
“Now our Tennessee angel is with the angels,” Wilson said before the performance. “Dolly, thank you for all you meant to us, and we will always love you.”
In the tribute, Gill and Wilson brought the crowd to their feet with their rendition of the ballad.
As the camera panned across the audience, several big stars including Luke Combs and Taylor Swift were seen getting emotional during the tribute.

Parton, whose country career spanned nearly 60 years, was a mainstay in both the genre and at the awards ceremony. Earning well over three dozen nominations, the “Jolene” singer took home 10 CMA awards, including the CMA’s Willie Nelson Lifetime Achievement Award in 2016

The Country Music Association, the organization behind the awards ceremony, previously held a two-hour celebration of the star’s legacy in October. The memorial featured a star-studded lineup of performances from Little Big Town to Kelsey Ballerini.

“At the end of the day, few artists define Country Music better than the one-word, Dolly. Over her decades-long career, I worked with her on a number of programs,” Sarah Trahern, CEO of the Country Music Association said in a press release. “She was always the most professional in every setting, often walking off the bus in heels and hair and makeup ready to go, before expected and before the cast and crew.”
Trahern added that in addition to Parton’s music, the community’s “biggest loss” is “her work as a philanthropist and the genuine difference she has made in people’s lives throughout the world.”
“There will only ever be one Dolly,” Trahern said.

title: Taylor Swift Lights Up CMA Awards Red Carpet With Striking Yellow Gown
summary: Taylor Swift arrived at the Country Music Association Awards in Nashville, Tennessee on Nov. 18 and immediately turned the red carpet into a fashion show, strutting her stuff in a striking yellow gown.
story: Taylor Swift may be associated with “Red,” but she can absolutely rock the color yellow.
Swift arrived at the Country Music Association Awards in Nashville, Tennessee on Nov. 18 and immediately turned the red carpet into a fashion show. She strutted her stuff in a striking yellow gown.
And while she’s scheduled to perform at the event, she doesn’t even need to do so to impress the internet.
Social media feeds quickly filled with comments from fans, declaring the singer a “goddess” and “queen.”
Swift’s ensemble features a high-low strapless dress from Oscar de la Renta’s Spring 2027 collection, paired with metallic gold heels. She finished the look with a classic updo and dangling earrings.
The “Patient Zero” singer’s return to the scheduled return to the stage marks her first performance at the ceremony in 13 years.
Swift is also nominated for single of the year for “I Knew It, I Knew You,” the singer’s 26th CMA award nomination.

title: Florence Pugh Calls Out Scrutiny of Her Appearance and Opens Up About Health Journey: ‘Happy and Truly Respecting My Body’
summary: Florence Pugh has a strong message for anyone who feels entitled to make unwelcome comments about her appearance.
story: Florence Pugh has a strong message for anyone who feels entitled to make unwelcome comments about her appearance.

On Nov. 18, the actor shared a lengthy statement on social media in response to rumors that she may have had plastic surgery or taken weight-loss medication. Pugh also shared a powerful message about her ongoing journey towards self-acceptance.
In the statement, the actor wrote that she “turned 30 and my New Year’s resolution was to change my relationship with alcohol, and to be able to do at least one pull up in the gym.”

“It’s funny to see you all use reference images from times where I was really mentally unhappy and abusing my body and put it next to the image from the governors awards the other night where I am happy and truly respecting my body,” Pugh said, referencing the chatter around her look at the Nov. 15 awards ceremony in Hollywood.
Pugh added that she has “f------ worked so hard to clean my head and clean my body because I don’t want to allow space for negativity in my mind to grow.”
“I’m looking after myself, and that’s literally it,” she wrote.

Pugh was seemingly referring to the content of a Nov. 17 Instagram Reel from Evie magazine on which she left a comment. In the reel, the magazine suggested that Pugh had “fallen victim to Hollywood’s war on round faces.”

“A lot of people are pointing out how Florence used to have full, beautiful cheeks that made her face super recognizable. Now that her jaw is more defined, her chin is more pointier, her jaws are more sharp, it makes sense why people are wondering if she’s had work done,” says Nikki Yabut, the Evie magazine content creator in the video.
Pugh commented on the post, slamming the discussion around her appearance.

“Guys. I turned 30. I’m a woman. Body’s and faces change,” Pugh wrote. “It’s not that deep, the fact that people can’t even tell between what’s aging and what’s surgery is disturbing. Sadly puppy fluff doesn’t last forever ❤️.”
In a statement provided to TODAY.com, Yabut said in part that she “never claimed” that Pugh had plastic surgery, “nor do I condone the harsh comments about her appearance.”

“I’ve always thought Florence was and is beautiful, and I admire her personality as well and how she uses her platform,” Yabut said in the statement, adding that she had intended to call out Hollywood’s normalizing of cosmetic procedures.

In her new Instagram post, Pugh referenced the widespread discussion of her appearance, saying that she finds it “so stressful” to wake up to “thousands of people talking about you and your body in ways that you can’t even comprehend.”

“I’m aware that the culture on socials currently is very interested in talking about people’s surgery and ozempic changes, it’s clearly a part of our time right now, that there’s this frenzy of people picking apart what’s truth and what’s fake,” she wrote.
She added that “quite a lot of you” were discussing her appearance in “such a disturbing way.”
“I learnt online that I had been on Ozempic?” she wrote. “I learnt that I’d had upper bleph? Lower bleph? Filler? Face lipo? Buc[c]al fat remover? Chin surgery? Nose surgery?!”
Pugh then questioned how “one person COULD get all of these things done over night.”

The 30-year-old noted that she’s spent her entire career  “defending and protecting bodies that just grow the way they grow” and said she was “subjected to fat shaming in the business”  since the beginning of her career.

Pugh also addressed the rumors head-on, saying she has never had face surgery and has never been on Ozempic. She went on to explain how any changes in her appearance are simply related to lifestyle changes she’s put into practice.
The actor wrote that she’s prioritized adding muscle this year, and can now do six pull ups and lift 110 kilograms.
Pugh pointed out how she has received “daily” comments about her body ever since she’s been in the public eye and encouraged people to be more sensitive.

“Let’s use this as a moment of self reflection. If you were one of those people that have the instinct to pull apart bodies, I think let’s start with asking yourself why? And what you get from it? And it’s ok to admit to yourself that it comes from something deeper. I’m not angry at you, I’m angry at the situation that’s being projected on to us,” she wrote.
“It feels inescapable, but part of changing the tide is on you as much as us in the public eye, she continued.

title: Christina Ricci Reveals Cher Is Holding a Nearly 30-Year ‘Grudge’ Against Her Over a Voicemail
summary: Christina Ricci says Cher has held a grudge for decades over an unreturned voicemail. The “Mermaids” star explained the rift on “Watch What Happens Live.”
story: Christina Ricci says she and Cher, her co-star in the 1990 film “Mermaids,” haven’t spoken in years due to a rift that started when Ricci was 19.

Ricci, 46, who played Cher’s younger daughter in the film when she was 9, told the story on the Nov. 17 episode of “Watch What Happens Live With Andy Cohen,” Bravo’s late-night talk show. Cohen asked whether she was still in touch with Cher, who is 80.
“I’m not,” she said. “Unfortunately, she’s still mad at me. She holds a grudge.”

The trouble began when a magazine interviewed Cher for a profile of the young actor. Ricci wasn’t sure whether it was Rolling Stone or Premiere, but she remembered Cher’s comments in it as “not that amazing about me,” she said.
Then came the phone call.
“She left me a voicemail about how journalists are always trying to get the worst things,” Ricci recalled, “and she was so sorry.
“And I was 19, and so I didn’t return that message,” she added.
Cohen asked if that was why Cher was upset. “I’m pretty sure,” Ricci said. She added that she tried to get in touch with Cher since then and hasn’t heard back.
Nearly three decades on, Ricci said she still “adores” Cher and has had time to think about it from the other end of the line.

“I absolutely, 100%, can imagine being Cher and being like, ‘Oh my God, they misquoted me, and I’m going to call this young person and explain to her,’” she said. “And then the gall of that young person to not return the call. I would be so pissed. I get it.”
TODAY.com has reached out to a representative for Cher for comment.

“Mermaids,” directed by Richard Benjamin, starred Cher as Rachel Flax, a restless single mother in the early 1960s who keeps moving her two daughters from town to town. Winona Ryder played the older daughter, Charlotte.
It was one of Ricci’s first film roles. She went on to star in “The Addams Family,” “Casper,” “The Ice Storm” and more recently, the Showtime drama “Yellowjackets.”
Before the segment ended, Ricci turned to the camera.
“Love you, Cher,” she said. “I love you so much.”

title: Druski Manifested His Comedy Success in a 2018 Tweet. He Reveals His Next Big Goal on TODAY
summary: Druski tweeted in 2018 his goal to be one of the biggest comedians in the world. Eight years later, he reveals his next lofty goal on TODAY.
story: Druski spoke his success into existence.

Before he landed a Netflix deal and before he became the youngest person to host the BET Awards and the first content creator to host “Saturday Night Live,” the 32-year-old posted a tweet back in 2018 about his ambitions.
“I will be 1 of the Biggest Comedians in the World .......,” he said.
The comedian, whose real name is Drew Desbordes, spoke to Craig Melvin, Al Roker and Dylan Dreyer on TODAY Nov. 18 about what prompted him to post that tweet.

“I’m big on manifesting,” he said. “I’ve always been one of those big believers that I write things down, and they come true. In that moment, I was very serious about that, and I was adamant, and I made it happen, so I’m grateful.”

Druski is coming off an “SNL” appearance that gave the show its highest rating in two years. His latest achievement is the upcoming release of his first Netflix special, a semi-scripted comedy series called “Collect & Praise” that drops on Dec. 1. Druski plays a money-hungry megachurch pastor with comedian Mike Epps as his scheming deacon in a series that Druski said was shot in less than two weeks.
He’s also appearing in his first movie role in 2027 in “The Catch,” an upcoming baseball romantic comedy starring Oscar winner Emma Stone and directed by Stone’s husband, Dave McCary.

“It was the first time in a long time I felt like a student again,” Druski said. “Being around just great actors and how good they are, watching how prepare and the small things they do, I’m just trying to learn.”
The experience also has him ready to manifest another lofty goal by speaking it out loud.
“Oh man, Oscar,” he said. “I got to get that Oscar! It’s on the way.”
He made the TODAY hosts echo his sentiment to help put it out into the universe. Al went a step further and said Druski is on his way to the coveted Oscar, Grammy, Tony and Emmy award superfecta.
“Druski, Oscar,” Al said. “Beginning of the EGOT.”
“Now we talking,” Druski said.

title: I Study James Bond for a Living. Here’s How I Reacted to the Robert Pattinson Casting (and Who I Would’ve Picked)
summary: What do James Bond experts think of Robert Pattinson’s casting?
story: “Take it From Me” is a TODAY series where experts use their wisdom to explain trends or make recommendations within their fields. In this, James Bond scholars weigh in on Robert Pattinson’s casting.
James Bond fans who waited seven long years to find out which actor would be the next to play the iconic British spy have gotten their answer.
Pattinson, Robert Pattinson.
Amazon MGM, which owns the rights to the Bond films, announced the choice on Nov. 16, which predictably left longtime fans either shaken or stirred.

Amazon founder Jeff Bezos revealed that he was involved in the decision at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World event in California. “We ran a really tight process and we made the final decision on Friday,” Bezos said, per NBC News reporting.

He added that there was a “big group” of actors who did “real, old-fashioned screen tests” to compete for the role. “There was something special about Rob and his performances,” Bezos said. “It was immediately un-debated. We all gravitated toward Rob.”

The 40-year-old star of “The Batman” and “The Odyssey” will succeed Daniel Craig, whose last Bond film was released in 2021. If the next Bond film is not released until 2028, it will have been the longest hiatus between movies in the franchise’s 64-year history, so the fans are thirsty for a new version.
TODAY.com discussed the casting choice with a trio of Bond scholars:

Oliver Buckton, the author of the Ian Fleming biography “The World Is Not Enough” and a professor and chair of the Department of English at Florida Atlantic UniversityColin Burnett, program director of Film & Media Studies at Washington University in St. Louis, and author of the forthcoming book “James Bond and the Art of Franchise Storytelling”James Chapman, the author of “Licence to Thrill: A Cultural History of the James Bond Films.”
Oliver Buckton, the author of the Ian Fleming biography “The World Is Not Enough” and a professor and chair of the Department of English at Florida Atlantic University
Colin Burnett, program director of Film & Media Studies at Washington University in St. Louis, and author of the forthcoming book “James Bond and the Art of Franchise Storytelling”
James Chapman, the author of “Licence to Thrill: A Cultural History of the James Bond Films.”
Here’s what they had to say.
A ‘Surprise’ Casting
Pattinson came on late as a candidate after it was previously reported that actors Callum Turner, Josh O’Connor, Jack Lowden and Nicholas Hoult had all undergone screen tests for the role in October.

“I was surprised, to be honest,” Buckton tells TODAY.com. “I think like a lot of people, we had in mind a shortlist that didn’t include him. But having time to think about it, it does make sense in a number of ways.”
“My immediate reaction was, ‘Wow, I wasn’t really expecting that,’ and then I got really excited about the idea,” Chapman says.
“At no point in history has a major A-list star been cast as James Bond at the peak of their career.”
Colin Burnett said on what makes Pattinson's casting remarkable
Burnett called Pattinson’s casting “a tectonic shift” in the way the role has been filled in the past.

“At no point in history has a major A-list star been cast as James Bond at the peak of their career,” Burnett says. “They have had reasonable careers, but Pattinson is someone who comes in aware of his stardom, of his box office potential, of his performance, and who’s very much going to look forward to steering the franchise. None of the previous actors had the clout on the way in to do that.”
Why Robert Pattinson’s Casting Makes Sense
The recurring theme that came up as to why Pattinson got the nod is simple: box office dollars.

Amazon MGM Studios took creative control of the Bond franchise in 2025 after making a deal with the franchise’s longtime producers, Michael G. Wilson and Barbara Broccoli. The change came four years after Amazon bought MGM, which owned the rights to the James Bond films, for $8.5 billion.

The online retail giant did not pay all that money to have the next Bond film to flop at the box office. That made going the traditional Bond route of casting an up-and-coming actor who is not yet widely known to the public, like Craig and former Bond actors Timothy Dalton and Pierce Brosnan, a gamble.

“I think that there’s so much at stake in this casting decision now with Amazon taking over and relaunching the whole franchise in a different way that they didn’t want to take a risk on an actor who hasn’t been in major films,” Buckton says.

“I know for a fact, having spoken to people inside Amazon, that they are hoping for and building the structure of Amazon MGM off a massive box office success (with Bond),” Burnett says. “What they’re hoping is to have a big hit right from the get-go, so that too is a major shift.”
Does Robert Pattinson Look the Part?

At 40, Pattinson is about the right age to play the superspy, who is generally considered to be in his late 30s, 40-ish in the Ian Fleming novels that made the character famous. The oldest actor to be cast as Bond was Roger Moore, who was 45 at the time.

Pattinson is also tall, lithe and dark-haired, which is closer to Fleming’s description of the character than Craig, who initially dealt with a wave of backlash about being blonde, short and muscular when he was first cast.
“People will feel just because of Pattinson’s look in a tuxedo with his hair back that he is James Bond, much more so than Daniel Craig,” Burnett says.
In an eerie coincidence, Pattinson resembles a cartoon rendering of Bond that Fleming had made in the late 1950s when he had a comic strip done of the character, according to Buckton.
“Fleming’s model was the 1930s star Hoagy Carmichael, but it looks uncannily like Robert Pattinson,” Buckton says.
Is Robert Pattinson Too Famous to Play Bond?
Will fans see James Bond on the screen or Robert Pattinson?

That is a question that has not been a problem for the six previous Bond actors, including the legendary Sean Connery, because they were not household names when they landed the role. The role made them famous.

“That’s the risk they’re taking, that he has too much baggage from other films,” Buckton says. “But he’s such a chameleon. Look at all the different roles he’s played, from ‘Twilight’ to ‘The Batman’ to movies like ‘The Lighthouse.’ I think they’re counting on him being able to do that again and reinvent himself as James Bond, and the fans will accept that.”
“The thing with Robert Pattinson is he changes with the times,” Burnett says. “He’s constantly reinventing himself.”

His experience in carrying big-budget films could actually be an asset rather than a drawback, according to the experts. It helps that he has already worked with director Denis Villeneuve on the “Dune” films because Villeneuve has committed to directing the next Bond film.

“He’s got that kind of crossover aspect to him,” Chapman says. “He’s done big franchise properties, big successful films with a female fanbase, so there’s real acting credentials there. He’s not a one-note actor. I’m thinking he can play Bond in a different way than he plays Batman.”
However, there’s also the possibility of overexposure if he’s also appearing in “Batman” and “Dune” movies in the midst of “Bond” films.

“Some of the negative reaction has been, let’s not have one actor taking on these iconic roles at the same time,” Buckton says. “That’s the risk, that Bond fans are like, ‘We want our own guy.  We want someone who’s not already Superman or Batman or whatever.’”
What Robert Pattinson Could Bring to the Role
Each of the previous six actors brought their own touch to the role, from the suave and sly Sean Connery to the campy Roger Moore to the brooding Daniel Craig.
Pattinson leaned in to a dark portrayal of Batman, so it remains to be seen how he balances the humor, physical prowess and romantic banter with the Bond girls in the new film.

“(Craig) became this wounded, dark, introspective James Bond, and I thought the new Bond would have to be a bit lighter,” Buckton says. “Even though (Pattinson) has played some dark characters, I think he has enough versatility. I would expect a little bit of a throwback to more of a suave, calm-under-pressure James Bond, and maybe a bit more of the Bond girl chemistry, which wasn’t Daniel Craig’s strong suit.”
“If Pattinson had come around and there had been no Craig, it would have been no problem to play more of a dark, psychological version, but Craig has cleared this ground already,” Burnett says.
Buckton speculated that maybe Pattinson’s performance in the Christopher Nolan movie “Tenet” could be a hint at what he does with Bond.
“I think that’s a glimpse of what he might be like because there’s something kind of edgy about him that I like, and maybe that’s what made him the choice,” he said.
Who Would Bond Experts Have Chosen?
Buckton liked “Superman” star Henry Cavill, 43, who was in the running for the role in the early 2000s as a 22-year-old but lost out to Craig.
Buckton would’ve gone with Callum Turner this time around.

“I could see him as Bond,” he says of Turner. “Some people say he didn’t have the charisma, but that’s something you can grow into. He could be identified as James Bond because he’s not a huge star right now, and I think he could bring that humor and a lighter touch to the role.”
Burnett would’ve gone with “Frankenstein” and “Wuthering Heights” star Jacob Elordi.

“I saw ‘Wuthering Heights’ in the theater and there’s a scene where he reemerges onscreen and the theater just swooned,” Burnett says. “That’s a star. That’s a thing Bond has always had. Men want to be like him and women want to be with him. Elordi has that feel.”

title: Walker Scobell Calls ‘Percy Jackson’ Season 3 ‘Most Accurate’ to the Books Yet
summary: Walker Scobell previews Season 3 of Disney+’s “Percy Jackson and the Olympians,” which will follow the events of “The Titan’s Curse” and majorly up the stakes.
story: Walker Scobell is ready for “The Titan’s Curse.” Percy Jackson, on the other hand, may not be.
“Be prepared,” Scobell tells TODAY.com. “It’s not like the other seasons... everything is a very real threat.”
With book and series fans alike anticipating Season 3 of “Percy Jackson and The Olympians,” set to release Nov. 20, the cast alludes to it as the series’ “darkest” addition yet.

Season 3 will follow the events of third book, “The Titan’s Curse.” With executive oversight by the series’ author, Rick Riordan, this will be the first time the third book has been adapted for the screen.

Riordan has been “involved in every writers room,” he told The Hollywood Reporter, much to the enthusiasm of book purists who were left disappointed by major changes in the Percy Jackson movie adaptations.

But Riordan isn’t the only one holding the TV adaptation to the book’s high standards. Scobell views the story from the perspective of its titular star and as a boy who first fell in love with the series at 9 years old.
“I would say it’s the most accurate season we’ve had, which was great for me,” Scobell tells TODAY.com.
To the 17-year-old, the more book-accurate the script is, the better.
“I almost sometimes wish I hadn’t read the books because, unfortunately, it’s hard for me to let it go,” he says.
“You know, there are things that have to change for (the show) to work,” he adds. “There’s also things that they’ve changed that have made it 10 times better.”
Previewing Season 3

“Percy Jackson and The Olympians” Season 3 will see Percy and an unlikely group of new characters journey across the country to find Annabeth (Leah Sava Jefferies) after she’s captured during their initial mission. Meanwhile, the threat of the demigod Luke (Charlie Bushnell), an impending war between the gods and titans and the great prophecy looms over Percy, who’s having to handle it all without Annabeth for the first time.
Like in previous seasons, this means viewers are in for plenty of epic showdowns — and on a grander scale than book readers may have originally envisioned, Scobell says.
“There are things we filmed that I was like, ‘Wow, this is so much bigger than it was in the books!’” he says.

It will also introduce some complicated new character dynamics, picking up with the cliffhanger at the end of Season 2. Thalia (Tamara Smart), the lost demigod daughter of Zeus, has returned to her human form after being turned into a tree years ago. This means that the great prophecy — which foretells that Olympus will be either saved or destroyed by a child of the big three gods (Zeus, Poseidon and Hades) — may not apply to Percy after all.

In the books, Percy and Thalia slowly establish a friendship, approaching each other with hesitancy but agreeableness. They also bond over the shared goal of saving Annabeth. But Scobell says that dynamic will look slightly different in Season 3, a change he says “works better” for the story’s arc.
“The only thing running through Percy’s head, in every single chapter in the book (is) ‘Annabeth, Annabeth, Annabeth,’” Scobell says.
In the show, Scobell’s character is driven by that same motivation, but the addition of Thalia adds “another level” of stakes to the quest.

“Now there’s this other girl, Thalia, who he doesn’t completely trust because they are so similar,” he adds. “It’s almost like he has to constantly choose what to focus on ... this ‘great prophecy’ with Thalia, or Annabeth.”
“I’m not going to spoil anything, but being so angry and intense at the beginning kind of carves out a nice story for the two of them,” he adds.

Thalia isn’t the only big three demigod Percy is going to have to look out for. “The Titan’s Curse” also famously introduces the di Angelo siblings, Bianca and Nico, to be played by Olive Abercrombie and and Levi Chrisopulos in Season 3. Fans of the book will remember that the Bianca and Nico turn out to be children of Hades.
“Levi, I mean ... he just looks like Nico,” Scobell says of his co-star. “Levi showed up, and he just kind of nailed it right away.”
As for how Percy will fare without Annabeth?
“Annabeth’s gone, yes, and her role in the trio ... she was the knowledgeable one on this whole world, right?” he says.

“You have Thalia and Grover, who have also had a lot of experience on the run,” he adds. “In a way, it’s kind of like that spot is, you know, not filled in, but there is someone there to to help make those decisions.”
More Star-Studded New Cast Members
Decisions, danger, and demigods aren’t the only things in store for our heroes. Another non-negotiable with quests? Run-ins with the gods of Olympus themselves, of course.

Joining the Olympian deities this season is Hera (Ming-Na Wen), Demeter (Jennifer Beals), Aphrodite (Kate McKinnon), Apollo (Hubert Smielecki) and Artemis (Dafne Keen). Season 3 will also be the first time since the show’s premiere that the gods will be seen altogether on Mount Olympus.
As intimidated as Percy is by the gods, so, too, was Scobell by his famous new co-stars.

“I had Jennifer Beals sign a ‘Flash Dance’ poster for me, and I had Ming-Na Wen sign a ‘Mulan’ poster for me,” Scobell says with a laugh. “That was the most nerve-wracking thing I think I’ve ever done on the set of ‘Percy Jackson.’”
What’s Next for Scobell?
As Season 3 debuts, Scobell is experiencing another life milestone: his junior year of high school.
“I don’t know if those two have ever really coincided very well,” he says.
“I don’t think I ever would have been able to do what I do without the help of my school, and then also the help of the set teachers I’ve been blessed with,” he adds.

As for what’s next, Scobell will appear in the upcoming “Angry Birds 3” movie, heading to theaters Dec. 23. He’s also hopeful for a “PJO” renewal for a fourth and fifth season. Scobell says the final two books in the series — “The Battle of the Labyrinth” and “The Last Olympian” — remain his favorites.
“I’ve always said (Book) 5, but you can’t really have the payoff of 5 without 4. So it’s like a ‘Avengers End Game—Infinity War’ situation,” Scobell says.
He also stresses that the show’s adaptation of “The Titan’s Curse” builds up the “intensity” that comes to a head in the final two parts of the story.

“There were points in filming the second and first season that I’m like, ‘I need to get hurt more,’ or like, ‘There needs to be a chance that I die on this quest,’” he says. “And with this, we’re narrowly escaping it every single time.”

title: Kathie Lee and Hoda Bring London Olympics to the Plaza in 2012
summary: Kathie Lee Gifford and Hoda Kotb competed in an obstacle course on the plaza in 2012 to help celebrate the Summer Olympics in London.
story: As TODAY marks its 75th anniversary, the TODAY Archive is revisiting legendary interviews, stories that moved us and other iconic moments from our 75 years on the air. These are the segments that shaped TODAY and created a lasting legacy. Today, we look back at Hoda and Kathie Lee competing in a wacky obstacle course to celebrate the Summer Olympics on July 27, 2012.
Kathie Lee Gifford and Hoda Kotb didn’t just get into the Olympic spirit while hosting the fourth hour of TODAY on July 27, 2012 — the same day that year’s Summer Olympics in London kicked off.
The pair put their athletic ability to the test in an obstacle course, as part of a celebration on the plaza for the Summer Games.

The duo, with a gaggle of interns behind them, walked onto the plaza, each carrying a glass of wine as the Olympic theme played. Hoda was decked out in a red tracksuit, as part of Team Hoda, while Kathie Lee sported blue for Team Kathie Lee. Guests applauded while young girls performed gymnastics.
How Did Hoda and Kathie Lee Hype Up the Obstacle Course?
The obstacle course was part of an all-Olympic-themed show.
“We have the most ridiculous, ridiculous obstacle course known to man,” Hoda said.
“I hear they’ve been taking bets on who’s going to win that one,” Kathie Lee said, prompting Hoda to say the bets were two-to-one for Kathie Lee.
“Where’s the outrage?” Hoda jokingly said.
“I don’t know. I don’t feel it today. It’s game day and I just don’t feel it,” Kathie Lee said.
What Did Hoda and Kathie Lee Have to Do on the Obstacle Course?
“This is going to show our ingenuity, our athletic ability,” Hoda said.
“All that stuff,” Kathie Lee added.
Entertainment Weekly’s Tim Stack was on hand to lay out what they’d have to do.
“This is a complicated course,” Hoda said.

The course featured a cornucopia of events, including spinning around a bat, carrying a glass of wine while walking across a balance beam, tossing a large ring like a hula hoop around an intern and slam dunking a basketball on a lowered basket.
“Hoda has a great advantage like that because she is 8 feet tall!” joked Kathie Lee.
They would also have to open a bottle of wine and race to be the first to put a medal around someone’s head at the end of the course.
How Did the Competition Go?
Kathie Lee took an early lead, but Hoda stormed back when she dunked. They were virtually tied when it came time to open the wine.
Kathie Lee had a cape put on her and was given a medal, which she successfully placed around the person’s neck, giving her the victory and earning her an oversized medal.
Hoda was hardly a sore loser, though.
“You guys, that rocked!” she said.

title: See Who Is Headed to the ‘DWTS’ Season 35 Finale After Stunning Elimination
summary: Read all about what went down during the Nov. 17 “DWTS” semifinals, including the dances, scores of each couple and who got eliminated.
story: It’s officially the semifinals on “Dancing With the Stars” and the six remaining couples are just a couple dances away from making it to the Season 35 finale.
The Nov. 17 episode kicked off with co-hosts Alfonso Ribeiro and Julianne Hough welcoming viewers to the second to last episode.
Last week saw the shocking and unexpected elimination of Jenna Dewan and partner Valentin Chmerkovskiy — and one more couple will take their last bow tonight.
Carrie Ann Inaba, Bruno Tonioli and Derek Hough are judging the last pairs as they each perform one final ballroom and Latin dance style to prove they are worthy of the Len Goodman Mirrorball Trophy.
A Recap of the Individual Dances

Connor Wood and partner Rylee Arnold were the first couple to compete and received mixed reactions. Bruno said that while he was bursting with excitement, he lost the timing towards the end. Carrie Ann told him to enjoy the moment more, while Derek did say he saw his excitement, but called some technical stuff out.
His second dance received more constructive criticism, while Carrie Ann got out of her seat to give him a hug and tell him he shouldn’t be nervous.

Harry Shum Jr. showed off his paso doble skills, delivering a fiery routine with Jenna Johnson that got Carrie Ann on her feet, calling it a “paso doble of the season.” Derek applauded him for his command and authority on the floor. For his second dance, a quickstep, Carrie Ann was blown away, while Derek said there was an intensity to Harry that had it all. Bruno called it “impeccable” in every way.

When it came to Maura Higgins’ samba, Derek called it “beautifully satisfying” and “impressive.” Bruno and Carrie Ann were utterly stunned by how she hit every move and executed it perfectly. For her Viennese waltz, Bruno called her haute couture and a beautiful way of showing her skills. Carrie Ann did note a strain in her neck, but still enjoyed the routine.

Ezra Frech’s quickstep got a round of applause from the audience and judges, who commented on his frame and momentum. Derek called him the definition of defying the odds. For his second dance, a jive, Carrie Ann got up and said it was so entertaining, Derek and Bruno also gave him his flowers for his accomplishments this season.

Amber Glenn’s salsa “lit up the ballroom,” according to Carrie Ann. Derek said she made a “statement” with her “professional-level routine,” while Bruno said it was “sal-sational.” The Olympian’s Viennese waltz had Carrie Ann telling her she “earned a spot in the finale” and Derek called it sultry and sensual and that she was the most consistent competitor. Bruno said she doesn’t miss a beat.

Closing out the first round was Tatyana Ali with a waltz that made her look like a “glittery goddess.” He also complimented her extensions and for listening to their feedback. Carrie Ann said her dancing makes people believe they too can dance beautifully. Her cha cha had Derek telling her she had great energy but did comment on some technical details like the foot placement, as did Bruno. Carrie Ann, however, called it perfection and gave them their first 10.

title: Jennifer Lopez Says She’s the ‘Happiest I’ve Been’ and Credits This 1 Change in Her Love Life
summary: Jennifer Lopez says she’s single, opens up about her divorces and the ‘JLo Show’ in new interview with Hoda Kotb on the TODAY show and podcast ‘Making Space.’
story: After decades in the public eye and four divorces, Jennifer Lopez is no stranger to love, both feeling and talking about it. The complex emotion was a major theme in her lengthy sit-down with friend and former TODAY anchor Hoda Kotb, which aired in part on TODAY Nov. 17. The full extended version will be available as an episode of  the “Making Space” podcast Nov. 18.

“The thing for me is to be the love in the room,” Lopez, 57, told Hoda, 62. “To put love out into the world. To remind people that love exists. ... Love yourself and remember who you are. I’ve been on that journey, and once you remember who you are, you wanna remind others. ... I feel like for me, since (I was) very young, without knowing it, that’s been my purpose.”

Hoda then revealed that one of the qualities she admires most about Lopez is her ability to fall in love. That prompted Hoda to share that she’s not sure if she’s ever been in love herself — “which gives me chills, and also makes me a little sad because it takes guts,” Hoda added.
“It takes a fearlessness,” Lopez responded before explaining why she’s fine without having romantic love at the moment.

“What you realize is what you’re searching for in another person is only up to you,” Lopez explained. “I have the ability to fall in love every day with my life, with the cup of coffee, with the bath, with the song I created that day.”
“The only way you really learn these lessons is to make mistakes, to fail, to have things not work out the way you thought they were.”
“It’s been kind of a two or three-year journey for me of really trying to understand myself, what my purpose is and what love is. And that for me has been a joy.”
She said she’s since realized that love isn’t what makes you happy, but rather that you should make yourself happy.

“You have to really understand that that is in your hands, and it’s how you wake up every day. ... It’s how you choose to walk through the world, understanding your power, understanding everything about yourself that is only you uniquely and what you have to offer to the world. And I think for me, that made me look at romantic relationships differently, as well, because it’s not something that I need. It’s something that I would like.”
“I have been the happiest I’ve been the past few years, where I’ve been single,” Lopez laughed. “But it took time to get there for me because I was such and I still am very much romantic.”
Lopez is now able to see the positive in this mindset though, she told Hoda.

“I used to beat that part of myself up. Like, that’s the reason I made these choices and these mistakes, and I’ve had these failures. ... I’ve been divorced several times. My kids didn’t have the things that I wanted them to have.”
“And then you realize ... that romantic is the person who is able to go out into the world and create a life that I could have never dreamed of when I was growing up in the Bronx.”

She said she sometimes struggled with how much of her personal life she made public. “I felt like it really overshadowed some of the work that I did and the things that I was really proud of ... And hurt me with opportunities as well, I think.”

“Your star celebrity part of you becomes bigger than the work that you’re doing. And I would look at other people’s careers and go, ‘Why don’t they get this type of scrutiny? Why is it me?’” she chuckled.

“I have to take responsibility in that I was very open about my life. I’ve never been kind of a guarded person in that way. I always wore my heart on my sleeve and was a very open book. And what I realize is that you have to have boundaries. That’s part of loving yourself. That’s part of it.”

A recent, major change in Lopez’s life that’s allowed her more time to reflect is becoming an empty nester. Her twins, whom she shares with ex-husband Marc Anthony, recently left for college. But, like any other parent, she helped them decorate their rooms, sobbed and went on her way.

“It was the first time I’ve lived alone in I don’t know how long, so that was really weird,” Lopez recalled. “Not having them down the hall does something to your heart. But I also realized I do enjoy my own company.”

“I enjoy my space, and I never was like that. I was always so afraid of the quiet and of being alone. I think that’s what drove me to make some decisions that weren’t the best for me in my life. But I really feel at peace there in my house that I’ve built.”
This major lifestyle change has helped inspire her in the recording studio, as well.

“I’ve made some songs that really feel very me right now. They’re a little bit unapologetic. They’re very different than things that I’ve dared to write before,” Lopez said. “A lot of 20-year-olds ... make the pop music. I made the pop music when I was in my 20s, and I write for me and for people who experience what I’m experiencing. And it’s a different type of feeling. I think it’s important to do that, to have that voice out there, too.”

The rom-com star is also focused on another creative project: the Thanksgiving Day release of her concert film, “The JLo Show: Live From Las Vegas.” The title is a play on how public her life has been over the past few decades.

“Yes, you’re watching ‘The JLo Show,’ me singing and dancing. But also, I started out watching ‘West Side Story’ on Thanksgiving in front of that TV, thinking about being an entertainer. I never thought that also my life, my personal life, would become the show and everything about me would be fair game,” Lopez explained.

“I didn’t think about the fame side of this. I just thought, ‘I wanna sing and dance and act. That’s what I wanna do with my life.’ This other part that comes along with it. And so, it’s a real, interwoven piece about a mini-musical of my life.”
So what’s next for the icon in her personal life? She told Hoda she’s setting boundaries and open to romantic partnership if it comes her way — but not just with anyone.

“You get to a point where you have a certain standard, because if I’m on the floor or if I’m up here, it doesn’t matter,” Lopez said. “Is there somebody who can match who you are and the love that you’re capable of giving?”
“Life is gonna take you in all those different directions, but having somebody who sees you and loves you in all of those iterations is really the goal.”

The full “Making Space” episode with Jennifer Lopez comes out November 18th. Watch it on YouTube or listen on Spotify. Check out Season 9 of “Making Space” for conversations with Ina Garten, Mariska Hargitay, Sandra Bullock and more!
